body.text: You may have the right qualifications.
You may have years of experience.
You may even be perfectly capable of doing the job you are applying for.
But if your CV does not communicate that value clearly, the recruiter may never find out.
This is one of the biggest misunderstandings I see among job seekers in Sri Lanka. Many people treat a CV as a document that simply lists education, work experience, skills, and personal information.
A professional CV should do much more than that.

Your CV is often the first professional introduction an employer receives from you. Before you attend an interview, speak to a hiring manager, or demonstrate what you can do, your CV has to create enough interest for the employer to take the next step.

That is why choosing the right **CV writing service in Sri Lanka** is not simply about making a document look attractive. Professional CV writing is about positioning your qualifications, experience, achievements, skills, and career direction in a way that both recruiters and modern hiring systems can understand.
If you are currently applying for jobs but receiving very few interview calls, the problem may not necessarily be your experience.
It could be the way your experience is being presented.
A Professional CV Is Not Just a Career History
One of the most common mistakes job seekers make is turning their CV into a complete employment history.

Technically, there is nothing wrong with these statements.
The problem is that they tell an employer very little about your actual value.
Hundreds of other candidates applying for similar roles may have performed exactly the same responsibilities.
A professionally written CV should answer a much more important question:
**Why should an employer consider you for this particular role?**
Instead of simply documenting everything you have done, your CV should identify and communicate the experience that is most relevant to the position you are targeting.
That is the difference between documenting your career and strategically presenting your career.
1. Your CV Should Make Your Career Direction Clear
A recruiter should not have to guess what type of position you are looking for.
Within the first part of your CV, it should become clear:

items: What type of professional you are
The industries or functions you understand
The type of position you are targeting
The value you could potentially bring to an employer

body.text: This is particularly important for professionals who have worked across several areas.
For example, someone may have experience in administration, customer service, sales, operations, and business development.
Simply listing all five areas equally can make the candidate appear unfocused.
Professional CV writing identifies the strongest career direction and positions supporting experience around that target.
This is one reason many job seekers choose to work with a **professional CV writer in Sri Lanka** rather than relying entirely on a generic CV template.
The objective is not simply better wording.
The objective is better positioning.
2. Your CV Should Be ATS-Friendly
Modern recruitment is increasingly technology-driven.
Many employers use Applicant Tracking Systems, commonly known as ATS, to collect, organise, search, and manage job applications.
This means a CV may interact with recruitment software before it receives detailed attention from a recruiter.
An **ATS-friendly CV** should therefore use a structure that allows important information to be identified clearly.

However, ATS optimization should never become keyword stuffing.
Adding dozens of keywords without context does not create a strong CV.

The better approach is to identify important terminology from the target role and naturally demonstrate those skills within your professional summary, experience, achievements, skills, projects, and other relevant sections.
A professional CV needs to work for **both technology and humans**.
Passing an automated system is meaningless if the recruiter who eventually reads the CV cannot understand your value.
3. Your CV Should Show Achievements, Not Only Responsibilities
This is one of the most important differences between an average CV and a strong professional CV.
Consider these two statements.
**Responsibility-focused:**
“Responsible for managing customer inquiries.”
**Value-focused:**
“Managed high-volume customer inquiries while resolving service issues and coordinating with internal teams to maintain timely customer support.”
The second statement provides more context about the candidate's contribution.
When possible, the impact becomes even stronger when measurable evidence is available.
For example:
“Managed 50+ daily customer inquiries while maintaining service quality and supporting timely resolution of escalated cases.”
Numbers are not mandatory for every bullet point.

But your CV should demonstrate scope, outcomes, improvements, responsibilities, complexity, leadership, revenue contribution, cost savings, efficiency, project delivery, customer impact, or another form of professional value wherever possible.
Your CV should not simply say:
**“This is what I was responsible for.”**
It should communicate:
**“This is what I contributed.”**
4. Your CV Should Be Relevant to the Job You Want Next
One CV should not necessarily be used for every vacancy.
Imagine someone with experience in:
Marketing Sales Business Development Customer Relationship Management Digital Marketing
That person applies for a Digital Marketing Executive role.
The employer is unlikely to give equal importance to every part of the candidate's background.
Digital campaigns, analytics, content strategy, paid advertising, lead generation, SEO, social media management, and campaign performance may be significantly more relevant.
A strong CV therefore prioritises information according to the target position.
This is known as **CV tailoring**.
It does not mean inventing experience.
It means presenting genuine experience according to its relevance to the opportunity.
The same professional may require slightly different positioning when applying for:
The candidate has not changed.
The employer's requirements have.
Your CV needs to recognise that difference.
5. Your CV Should Be Easy for a Recruiter to Scan
Recruiters do not initially approach every CV like a book.
They scan.
They look for information that helps them quickly determine whether a candidate deserves further attention.
Your CV therefore needs a strong information hierarchy.
Important information should not be buried inside long paragraphs.

Design should support readability rather than compete with the content.
A CV can look professional without using excessive colours, graphical skill bars, complicated columns, large decorative elements, photographs, or unnecessary visual effects.
The objective is not to win a graphic design competition.
The objective is to win an interview.
6. Your CV Should Present the Right Level of Seniority
A fresh graduate CV should not be written like an executive CV.
Likewise, someone with 15 years of leadership experience should not present their career in the same way as someone entering the workforce.
Different career stages require different positioning.

7. Your CV Should Support Your Personal Brand
Your CV does not exist in isolation anymore.
Employers may also review your LinkedIn profile, online portfolio, GitHub profile, professional website, publications, or other digital presence.
Your CV and LinkedIn profile should therefore tell the same fundamental career story.
If your CV positions you as a Data Analyst while your LinkedIn profile still presents you as an Administrative Assistant, the inconsistency can weaken your professional positioning.
The same applies to your cover letter.
Ideally, your:
**CV + Cover Letter + LinkedIn Profile**
should work together as one professional career branding system.
Your CV establishes your qualifications and evidence.
Your cover letter explains your relevance and motivation.
Your LinkedIn profile strengthens your professional visibility and credibility online.
This is why professional career services increasingly extend beyond CV writing alone.

A rejected application does not automatically mean the candidate was unqualified.

Professional CV writing should not involve simply replacing your words with more complicated English.
It should involve understanding your career, identifying the strongest evidence, researching the target role, structuring the information, and communicating your value clearly.
How to Choose a CV Writing Service in Sri Lanka
Before paying someone to write your CV, look beyond the design.
Ask whether the service considers:

**Career positioning:** Does the CV clearly communicate the role you are targeting?

faqs.question: Is a professionally written CV guaranteed to get me a job?
faqs.answer: No legitimate CV writer can guarantee a job. A professional CV can improve the way your qualifications, experience, skills, and achievements are presented, but hiring decisions depend on many factors including experience, qualifications, competition, interview performance, salary expectations, location, and employer requirements.

faqs.question: How long should a professional CV be?
faqs.answer: There is no universal page count that applies to every candidate. The correct length depends on career stage, experience, industry, and the relevance of the information. The priority should be relevance and clarity rather than artificially forcing a CV into a particular number of pages.

faqs.question: Should I use the same CV for every job?
faqs.answer: Your core CV can remain consistent, but important sections should ideally be tailored according to the position being targeted. This can include the professional summary, competencies, terminology, ordering of information, and emphasis placed on particular achievements.

faqs.question: Do I need both a CV and LinkedIn profile?
faqs.answer: They serve different purposes. Your CV is primarily an application document. LinkedIn functions as a professional digital profile, networking platform, personal branding tool, and recruiter discovery channel. Using both strategically can create stronger overall career positioning.

faqs.question: Is ATS optimization only important for overseas jobs?
faqs.answer: No. Applicant Tracking Systems and digital recruitment platforms are increasingly relevant across modern hiring environments. Even where a sophisticated ATS is not used, the principles behind ATS-friendly writing—clear structure, relevant terminology, readability, and consistent information—also make a CV easier for recruiters to evaluate.

What a CV maker can do well

A builder can provide consistent headings, spacing and downloadable files. If you already have strong achievements, accurate dates and a clear target role, a straightforward template may be sufficient. Check the export before committing: can you edit the document later, and does the downloaded version contain readable text?

The limitation is that a template cannot verify your contribution. A box labelled “Experience” will accept a vague duty just as readily as a strong example. Attractive formatting does not make the underlying evidence more relevant.
What you should expect from a writer

A writer should ask about the roles you want, the work you actually performed and the results you can support. They should help distinguish your contribution from your team's results, explain unfamiliar industry terminology and decide which older information deserves less space.

For example, “handled stock” needs clarification before rewriting. Did you reconcile inventory, investigate discrepancies, receive deliveries or coordinate replenishment? The answer determines the skills and evidence the CV should show.
Compare the deliverables, not the label
Before buying either option, check:

items: Whether the final file is editable and the download has additional charges.
Whether the service includes content rewriting or only layout changes.
Whether someone checks the CV against your intended role.
Whether revisions and turnaround expectations are explained.
Whether your personal information is handled appropriately.

A practical way to choose

Try drafting your summary and three recent achievements without a template. If the information is specific and clearly relevant, start with a simple builder. If you cannot decide what to emphasise, or you are changing careers, consider a review or a writing service.

You can also combine the approaches: develop accurate content with professional feedback, then maintain it in an editable document. Keep a master copy so that future applications do not depend on continued access to a paid platform.

items: An initial discussion or questionnaire about your background.

body.text: A CV can become outdated even while your career is progressing. These ten signs help you decide whether minor edits are enough or a deeper rewrite would help.
Use them as a document review, not as a diagnosis of every unsuccessful application. A rejection does not prove that your CV caused the outcome.
Check the direction and opening

items: **Your target role is unclear.** If your opening could introduce an accountant, salesperson or administrator equally well, replace general ambition with a specific professional direction.
**Your summary describes an earlier career stage.** A profile written for your first job may now hide supervisory experience or specialist knowledge.
**Your strongest evidence appears too late.** Relevant projects, qualifications and achievements should be easy to locate without reading every page.

body.text: An opening does not need dramatic language. It needs to give the reader a useful interpretation of the evidence that follows.
Review the experience section

items: **Every bullet begins with a duty.** “Responsible for reports” says little about the audience, decisions or improvements involved.
**Different roles sound identical.** Repeated bullets can conceal promotions, increasing complexity and greater independence.
**Results are unsupported or exaggerated.** If you cannot explain where a percentage came from, investigate or replace it with an accurate description of scope.

body.text: For example, “improved operations” could become “introduced a weekly handover log so the next shift could track unresolved customer requests.” That is more specific without inventing a numerical result.
Inspect relevance and usability

items: **Old information dominates.** Detailed school activities may crowd out recent professional achievements.
**The file is difficult to edit or read.** Broken page breaks, overlapping text and inconsistent dates need attention before another application.
**You send the same emphasis to unrelated roles.** An account-management application and an operations application may use the same facts but need different priorities.
**Your CV contradicts LinkedIn or the application form.** Check titles, dates, qualification status and claims about responsibility across all three.

body.text: Decide what level of help you need

Mark each issue as a factual correction, a formatting issue or a positioning problem. Several small formatting corrections may be manageable yourself. If the document no longer tells the right career story, rewriting is more useful than changing colours or fonts.

Before seeking help, gather a recent job advertisement, your current CV and notes about achievements omitted from it. That gives a reviewer something concrete to assess and reduces the risk of receiving generic advice.

Tell the writer which roles, industries and countries you are considering. Ask how those choices will affect the CV. A writer who cannot explain the intended audience may produce a polished document with weak relevance.

Ask whether there is a questionnaire, consultation or opportunity to clarify your background. The writer should distinguish individual achievements from team outcomes and check unclear dates or qualification status with you.

Look for clear summaries, specific experience and readable structure. A sample can demonstrate writing decisions without exposing another client's contact details. Ask what changed between the original information and the finished version.

The provider should explain document readability and relevant terminology in ordinary language. Ask what any advertised score measures and which tool produces it. A third-party score is not a universal decision made by every employer's recruitment system.

Confirm the file formats, number of role variants, delivery period and revision process. Clarify whether a revision corrects the agreed CV or includes rewriting it for a completely different profession. Both parties benefit from a clear scope.

A writer normally needs career details and contact information for the document. Ask before supplying identity documents, confidential financial records or other people's personal information. Ask what happens if you are unhappy with the draft and where the relevant service terms are published. Read any guarantee carefully: a revision promise is different from a promise that an employer will interview you.

body.text: A professionally written CV can make your experience easier to understand and your applications more focused. Its value comes from clearer evidence and better decisions.

It does not create qualifications, remove eligibility requirements or guarantee a response. For Sri Lankan job seekers, the useful question is what changes in the document and how those changes support the next application.
It can clarify what you are applying for

People with varied experience often describe everything equally. A candidate who has worked in retail, administration and customer support might present three unrelated histories. A stronger approach identifies the target role and selects the relevant thread, such as customer operations and service coordination.
The facts stay the same. The opening summary and order of emphasis help the recruiter interpret those facts in relation to the vacancy.
It can uncover evidence you overlooked

Routine work often contains useful achievements. Creating a handover checklist, training a new colleague or resolving recurring invoice errors may demonstrate valuable skills even when the employer did not issue a formal award.

A writer should ask what changed, what you personally did and how you know the result. That conversation may produce stronger bullets than simply replacing everyday verbs with impressive-sounding alternatives.

For example, “helped new staff” becomes more informative when it explains that you prepared training notes and guided new colleagues through order processing. Numbers should be added only when you can verify them.
It can reduce friction in each application

A well-organised master CV makes tailoring easier. You can identify which achievements belong in a specific version, keep the factual history consistent and avoid rebuilding the document from scratch.
An editable file also matters. You should be able to add a certification or promotion without disrupting every page. Ask the writer to explain the structure and which areas you can adjust safely.
It can strengthen your interview preparation

The final CV becomes a set of claims an interviewer may explore. Review every bullet and prepare to explain the context, your contribution and the result. If you do not understand the wording, revise it before submitting the document.
This step prevents a common problem: a polished CV that sounds unlike the candidate and contains claims they cannot comfortably discuss.
Use the improvement as part of a wider search

Keep a record of vacancies, versions sent and outcomes. Combine relevant applications with appropriate networking and preparation. If a particular type of role produces no response, reassess fit and evidence instead of repeatedly changing the design.

Explore [professional CV writing](/services/packages/cv-writing) if your career story needs restructuring. A [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) can be a more focused starting point when the existing document is already close to what you need.

Adapt the same facts for different uses

Consider a lecturer applying for both a teaching position and a corporate training role. The academic version may need publications and teaching history. The corporate version may emphasise workshop design, participant needs and evaluation of learning.

content: An ATS-friendly CV helps recruitment software and people interpret your career information. It is a practical writing and formatting approach, not a hiring guarantee. Sri Lankan candidates may encounter different application portals for local and overseas jobs. Instead of trying to defeat an unknown system, prepare a clear document and follow the instructions of the employer receiving it.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: An ATS-friendly CV helps recruitment software and people interpret your career information. It is a practical writing and formatting approach, not a hiring guarantee.

Sri Lankan candidates may encounter different application portals for local and overseas jobs. Instead of trying to defeat an unknown system, prepare a clear document and follow the instructions of the employer receiving it.
Understand the separate stages

An applicant tracking system can store applications and support recruitment workflows. Parsing is the extraction of information from a document into fields. Screening may also involve application questions or employer-defined criteria. These are related activities, but they are not the same decision.

Greenhouse documents cases where a resume remains attached even when automatic extraction fails. A parsing problem should therefore not be described as automatic rejection in every system. See [Greenhouse's parsing guidance](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200989175-Unsuccessful-resume-parse).
Build a document that is easy to interpret

Use familiar headings such as Professional Summary, Experience, Education and Skills. Associate each role clearly with an employer and dates. Keep essential contact details in the main document and avoid replacing meaningful text with icons.

Before submitting, select and copy the text into a plain document. Inspect the reading order and check that names, dates and important skills remain visible. This is a useful diagnostic, although it does not reproduce every employer's software.
Match terminology with real evidence

Read the vacancy for specific tools, responsibilities and qualifications. If it asks for bank reconciliation and you have performed that work, name it where the experience appears. Do not substitute vague wording such as “finance activities” when a precise, accurate term is available.

A skills section should summarise capabilities you can explain. Your experience and projects should show where you used them. Hidden text, copied advertisements and repeated keywords undermine the document's credibility.
Inspect the application, not just the file

After upload, check any fields the portal fills automatically. Correct errors where the application allows it. Answer eligibility questions honestly and attach the requested file type, rather than relying on a blanket rule about PDF or Word.
Keep a saved copy of the version submitted. If an employer contacts you later, you should know exactly which claims and examples they have seen.
A sensible next step

Review one target vacancy beside your CV. Mark missing evidence, unclear headings and unsupported claims separately. The [ATS CV audit tool](/tools/ats-cv-audit) can support a review, while [professional CV writing](/services/packages/cv-writing) can help restructure content. Neither should be treated as proof that an employer will shortlist you.

faqs.question: Do all employers use the same ATS rules?
faqs.answer: No. Systems, configurations and hiring processes vary. Follow the specific application instructions and keep your document clear.

faqs.question: Does ATS-friendly mean removing all design?
faqs.answer: No. Readable typography, spacing and restrained visual hierarchy can make a CV professional without relying on complicated layouts.

content: An ATS is an applicant tracking system. It helps employers manage applications, but saying that “the ATS rejected my CV” can hide several different events. Some hiring workflows use automatic screening. Others rely on people reviewing applications. Without information from the employer, you cannot reliably infer the reason for rejection from the speed of the response alone.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: An ATS is an applicant tracking system. It helps employers manage applications, but saying that “the ATS rejected my CV” can hide several different events.

Some hiring workflows use automatic screening. Others rely on people reviewing applications. Without information from the employer, you cannot reliably infer the reason for rejection from the speed of the response alone.
Separate parsing from screening

Parsing extracts information such as names, employers and dates from a file. Screening evaluates an application against criteria. A document can parse correctly while the candidate does not meet an essential requirement; a parsing error does not necessarily mean the application disappears.

This distinction matters because rewriting keywords will not resolve every problem. The issue might involve an application answer, a mandatory qualification, a closed vacancy or a decision made by the hiring team.
Review questions carefully
Employers may ask about availability, location, required credentials or permission to work. Read the wording before answering. Do not change truthful answers to try to avoid a filter.

For example, being willing to relocate is different from already living in the employer's city. Similarly, studying toward a qualification is different from having completed it. Make those distinctions clear in both the form and the CV.
Make the file straightforward
Keep role titles, employer names and dates together. Use searchable text and follow the accepted upload formats. Avoid a scanned image when a text-based document is requested or supported.

If the application extracts your employment history into fields, check those fields before submitting. A missing date or incorrectly merged employer can often be corrected at that stage. Save the confirmation when the portal provides one.
Do not diagnose rejection from a score

An online checker may compare your document with a job advertisement using its own method. That number does not reveal the employer's screening configuration or whether someone read the application. Treat specific observations as editing suggestions and question unsupported promises.

Use a simple review log: vacancy, essential requirements, evidence submitted and outcome. Patterns can guide improvements, but they still need interpretation. A response from a recruiter is stronger evidence about their process than speculation about an invisible algorithm.
Focus on what you can improve

Choose suitable roles, communicate evidence clearly and submit complete applications. If you need a document review, bring an actual vacancy and your answers to relevant application questions. That creates a more useful discussion than asking someone to “beat the ATS.”
The [CV review service](/services/packages/cv-review) can help assess presentation and relevance. It cannot reveal a private employer's decision rules.

faqs.question: Does a quick rejection prove that a robot rejected me?
faqs.answer: No. Timing alone does not identify the decision-maker or the reason. Consider the whole application and any employer feedback.

faqs.question: Can I bypass screening with hidden keywords?
faqs.answer: Do not use hidden text. It creates misleading content and does not address eligibility or provide credible evidence of your skills.

content: A polished CV should remain understandable when its visual decoration is removed. Testing the exported file helps you find problems that are easy to miss on screen. You do not need access to an employer's system to perform basic checks. You do need to recognise their limits: a successful text copy is useful evidence of readability, not certification for every ATS.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: A polished CV should remain understandable when its visual decoration is removed. Testing the exported file helps you find problems that are easy to miss on screen.

You do not need access to an employer's system to perform basic checks. You do need to recognise their limits: a successful text copy is useful evidence of readability, not certification for every ATS.
Inspect the document in two ways
First, read the CV visually. Check whether headings, role dates and important achievements are easy to locate. Then copy its text into a plain document and read it from the beginning.

Does the first employer still connect to the correct title? Do dates appear beside the right roles? Has a sidebar interrupted the middle of a sentence? Record the actual problem instead of assuming that every attractive layout is unsafe.
Watch for information carried only by graphics
An email icon does not replace the email address. A row of stars does not explain proficiency in Excel. A company logo does not identify an employer as clearly as its written name.

Replace visual skill ratings with meaningful descriptions. “Excel: pivot tables, reconciliation worksheets and lookup formulas” gives a reader more usable information than “Excel: 90%.” Include only skills you can demonstrate.
Keep important relationships intact

Try putting employer, role and dates in a consistent sequence. Use ordinary text for the information that determines your professional history. If you retain a sidebar, ensure that it does not carry the only copy of essential details or disrupt the exported reading order.

Greenhouse lists complex formatting among possible parsing problems, which is a reason to test your document rather than judge it only by appearance. See [its troubleshooting notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200989175-Unsuccessful-resume-parse).
Recheck after every export

The file you edit and the file you upload may behave differently. Open the final PDF or Word document, check every page and test its links. Look for split bullets, missing symbols and text that has become too small.
Ask someone unfamiliar with your career to identify your target role and strongest relevant achievement. If they cannot, the issue may be information hierarchy rather than technical extraction.
Keep design working for you

Use spacing, bold headings and a restrained accent colour to guide attention. Keep a separate portfolio for visual work when useful. The CV can link to that portfolio while staying easy to read and update.
If your document needs a second pair of eyes, request a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) and include the actual exported file, not just a screenshot of the design.

faqs.question: Is every two-column CV unreadable?
faqs.answer: No. Results depend on the document and processing system. Test the reading order and simplify layouts that scramble information.

faqs.question: Should I submit a screenshot of my CV?
faqs.answer: Use the employer's requested format. A screenshot can make text extraction and editing harder than a properly exported text-based document.

author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: ATS CV mistakes include both document problems and misleading content. Review these fifteen issues before assuming that a missing keyword explains every rejection.
The list is a practical editing tool. It does not claim that every employer uses the same software or that each mistake automatically causes rejection.
File and layout problems

items: **Ignoring the requested file type.** Follow the vacancy or upload instructions first.
**Submitting an image instead of readable text.** Check whether you can select the words in the exported file.
**Leaving a broken reading order.** Copy the text elsewhere and inspect how columns or floating elements are read.
**Using icons without written contact details.** Make your email and phone number unambiguous.
**Hiding essential content in decorative elements.** Keep role history and qualifications in ordinary document text.

body.text: Always inspect the uploaded version where a preview is available. A good source document does not guarantee a clean export.
Structure and factual problems

items: **Unclear section headings.** “My journey” is less precise than “Professional Experience.”
**Dates detached from roles.** Associate each date range with the correct employer and title.
**Inconsistent employment history.** Compare the CV with the application form and LinkedIn.
**Unexplained internal job titles.** Add a truthful functional description when a company-specific title would confuse an outsider.
**Incorrect qualification status.** Distinguish completed, ongoing and planned study.

body.text: A clear structure also benefits the human reader. Fixing factual relationships is more important than chasing a cosmetic score.
Relevance and credibility problems

items: **Omitting a skill you actually used.** Name relevant tools and responsibilities precisely.
**Copying an entire advertisement.** Demonstrate the requirements through your own experience instead.
**Adding skills you cannot defend.** A keyword may create an interview question you cannot answer.
**Repeating the same words without evidence.** One contextual example is more useful than several unsupported mentions.
**Assuming a checker score guarantees shortlisting.** Different tools measure different things; the employer makes the decision.

body.text: Fix the most consequential issues first

Work through the CV in three passes: factual accuracy, relevance to the vacancy, then file presentation. This prevents spending an hour aligning headings while leaving an incorrect date or missing requirement unresolved.

Keep a clean master document and a record of each application version. After substantial changes, ask someone to read the CV without your explanations and describe what they understand about your career.
The [ATS CV audit tool](/tools/ats-cv-audit) can support a structured review. For help selecting evidence and rewriting unclear content, compare [CV writing services](/services/packages/cv-writing).

faqs.question: Should I fix all fifteen issues even if the portal accepted my file?
faqs.answer: Fix any that apply. Successful upload does not establish factual accuracy, relevance or the quality of the reading experience.

faqs.question: Can these checks guarantee interviews?
faqs.answer: No. They improve application quality, while shortlisting still depends on suitability, competition and the employer's process.

content: Writing an ATS-friendly CV starts with a clear target role and evidence of relevant work. Useful terminology should help a recruiter understand your experience. Do not treat the document as a collection of search terms. A CV that names the right tools but never explains how you used them may be easy to search and difficult to evaluate.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha
keywords: how to write ATS friendly CV

body.text: Writing an ATS-friendly CV starts with a clear target role and evidence of relevant work. Useful terminology should help a recruiter understand your experience.
Do not treat the document as a collection of search terms. A CV that names the right tools but never explains how you used them may be easy to search and difficult to evaluate.
Make a requirement-to-evidence worksheet

Read one representative vacancy and identify its main responsibilities, tools and qualifications. For each, write a real example from your experience. Separate direct evidence, transferable evidence and genuine gaps.

For a finance role, the worksheet might connect bank reconciliation to your monthly reconciliation work, Excel to a reporting workbook and audit support to preparing supporting schedules. Do not label a gap as experience simply because the keyword appears in the advert.
Use recognisable, accurate terms

Write the normal name of a tool or skill where it belongs. If an acronym could be unclear, include the full term once. Avoid renaming genuine roles to make them appear more senior; a short functional explanation is safer when your internal title is unfamiliar.
For example, “Operations Associate — customer order coordination” can explain a broad title if the description is accurate. The official title remains visible for reference checks.
Show the skill in action

Replace “SQL, SQL reporting, SQL analysis” with one specific example such as “used SQL queries to reconcile weekly order records and investigate missing transactions.” This illustrates the activity and purpose without claiming an unsupported outcome.
List important capabilities in the skills section, then support them in employment or project descriptions. Repetition is useful only when it adds context.
Keep the structure predictable
Use clear headings and a consistent role format. Put contact details in readable text. Follow file-type instructions and inspect the final document after export.

When an application form imports information, check the populated fields. Correct a misplaced employer or missing qualification if the portal allows it. The file and the form should tell the same factual story.
Review for a person as well as software

Ask whether the opening identifies your professional direction and whether the first relevant role shows concrete work. Remove words that add length without meaning. A reader should not have to decode internal abbreviations or infer your contribution from a list of tools.

Use the [free career resources](/resources) to begin a draft, or seek [CV writing support](/services/packages/cv-writing) when you need help translating experience into clear evidence. The goal is accurate relevance, not an artificial keyword density.

faqs.question: Should every keyword appear several times?
faqs.answer: No fixed repetition count applies. Use a term where it helps identify or explain genuine experience, and remove unnecessary duplication.

faqs.question: Can I include skills I am currently learning?
faqs.answer: Yes, when relevant and clearly labelled as learning or project experience. Do not imply professional proficiency you have not developed.

Avoid deciding by the name of the design tool alone. A simple export can be easier to interpret than a complicated document created in a word processor. Inspect the result you will actually submit.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: A CV made in Canva is not automatically unsuitable for an ATS. What matters is the finished file: its text, reading order, structure and relevance.
Avoid deciding by the name of the design tool alone. A simple export can be easier to interpret than a complicated document created in a word processor. Inspect the result you will actually submit.
Choose the layout before decorating

Start with one clear reading path. Give work history enough space, keep dates beside the right roles and use written labels for contact details. Avoid choosing a design that forces you to remove important evidence to make it fit.

A template's sample content is not a recommended CV length. If the design contains only two short experience boxes, that does not mean your professional history should be compressed into two vague sentences.
Test the exported file
Open the download in a separate viewer. Try selecting and copying the text into a plain document. Check whether your name, email, employers, role titles and dates appear in a sensible order.

If content is missing or jumbled, simplify the design and export again. This test is a useful warning system, not a simulation of every ATS. Follow any file requirements stated by the employer even if your preferred design tool exports a different format.
Replace visual ratings with meaningful evidence

Skill bars and stars do not explain what you can do. “Power BI: data preparation, dashboard development and stakeholder reporting” is more informative than a four-star rating when those capabilities are accurate.
Similarly, a decorative headline such as “creative problem solver” needs support. A brief project description can demonstrate the problem, your contribution and what was delivered.
Keep an editable master

Think about future updates before submitting your first version. Can you add a promotion, change a target role or supply a requested document format without rebuilding the CV? Keep a factual master record outside any particular visual template.

For design-related roles, link to a portfolio that shows your visual work. Your application CV can remain restrained while the portfolio carries richer examples. Test that portfolio links open correctly and do not require unexpected access permissions.
Decide based on the application

If the employer specifies a format or provides a template, follow it. Otherwise, choose a file that remains readable, easy to update and suitable for the role. A [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) should assess both the writing and the exported document, rather than approving or rejecting it solely because it was made in Canva.

faqs.question: Must I stop using Canva for my CV?
faqs.answer: No. Evaluate your specific layout and export. If the file is hard to read or adapt, move the content into a simpler document.

faqs.question: Does a clean text-copy test prove ATS compatibility?
faqs.answer: No. It helps identify extraction and reading-order problems, but different recruitment systems may process the same file differently.

content: Good ATS CV formatting keeps career information connected and readable. Consistency matters more than decorative complexity or a supposedly perfect template. Use the following rules to build a document you can maintain. They are practical defaults, and an employer's explicit instructions should take priority.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Good ATS CV formatting keeps career information connected and readable. Consistency matters more than decorative complexity or a supposedly perfect template.
Use the following rules to build a document you can maintain. They are practical defaults, and an employer's explicit instructions should take priority.
Create a clear information hierarchy

Place your name and contact details first, followed by a relevant profile and the strongest evidence for your career stage. Use familiar section headings. Keep employer, title, location where useful and dates together in each experience entry.
Do not rely on position alone to explain relationships. A date floating in a distant sidebar may look aligned on one screen but become confusing when text is extracted or the page layout shifts.
Make styles consistent

Choose one body font and a small number of heading styles. Use the same date pattern across roles and education. Keep bullet spacing and indentation consistent so the reader can concentrate on the content.
Treat bold text as a guide, not a decoration for every second phrase. If everything is emphasised, nothing stands out. Avoid shrinking the body text simply to preserve an arbitrary page count.
Keep meaningful information as text
Write email addresses, phone numbers, tools and qualifications plainly. Do not communicate skill levels solely with graphics. Avoid placing the only copy of essential information in a shape or image.
A useful skills entry explains capability: “Excel: pivot tables and monthly reconciliation workbooks.” It is clearer than a percentage that has no defined measurement behind it.
Control page breaks deliberately

Check that a role heading is not separated from all its bullets. Look for a second page containing only a few lines or an education entry split awkwardly across pages. Use paragraph and page-break controls instead of repeatedly pressing Enter to force alignment.
Reopen the exported file after changes. Editing software and viewers can show layout differently, so the final download deserves its own review.
Verify the submitted version

items: Open every page and check spacing, symbols and links.
Copy the text into a plain document and inspect its order.
Confirm the file type and size meet the portal's stated requirements.
Review auto-filled application fields before submitting.
Keep the exact version you sent.

body.text: These checks reduce avoidable presentation problems. They do not guarantee a hiring outcome or compensate for missing evidence. For a structured starting point, explore the [free CV resources](/resources); for a document-specific assessment, use [CV review support](/services/packages/cv-review).

faqs.question: Is one font mandatory?
faqs.answer: No. Consistency and legibility are the goals. Using one font is simply an easy way to avoid unnecessary visual variation.

faqs.question: Are all tables forbidden?
faqs.answer: No universal rule covers every document and system. If a table makes reading order or editing unreliable, replace it with ordinary paragraphs.

author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: The right CV keywords describe requirements you can actually meet. Start with real vacancies and connect each important term to evidence from your background.
Keyword research for a job application is not the same as adding popular words to attract attention. You need the language of the role and a truthful reason for using it.
Read beyond the job title

Two “Operations Executive” roles may involve different work. One could emphasise order processing and customer coordination; another could focus on inventory and warehouse reporting. Read responsibilities, essential requirements and preferred experience separately.

Select a small group of closely related vacancies to understand recurring terms. Do not combine unrelated advertisements into one giant skills list. The actual application should still respond to the specific opening.
Sort terms into useful groups

items: **Tools:** software, equipment and systems you have used.
**Activities:** tasks such as reconciliation, scheduling or requirements gathering.
**Knowledge:** relevant methods, standards or subject areas.
**Credentials:** qualifications and licences, with accurate status.
**Context:** industries, customers or operating environments you understand.

body.text: For each term, note where you gained the experience and what you can explain in an interview. Leave out words that sound relevant but have no evidence behind them.
Distinguish essential and optional requirements
An essential credential may determine eligibility; a preferred tool may be something the employer is willing to teach. Do not interpret every word in an advert as equally important.

If you have adjacent experience, describe it precisely. Experience with one reporting tool can demonstrate transferable analytical work, but it is not the same as professional experience with a different named tool.
Place keywords in context

A data candidate might write, “Built a Power BI dashboard from cleaned sales data to help the team compare regional performance.” That sentence identifies a tool, activity and purpose. It is more informative than listing “Power BI” several times.
Use a compact skills section for quick reference, and experience or project bullets for evidence. Include the full term and acronym together when useful, then write naturally.
Review for honesty and readability
Read the completed CV aloud. If a phrase exists only to repeat a keyword, remove or rewrite it. Ask whether you could explain every named skill through a specific task or project.

Keep your keyword worksheet alongside your master CV. It becomes a practical tailoring aid for future applications. The [CV writing service](/services/packages/cv-writing) can help organise this evidence, while the [ATS audit tool](/tools/ats-cv-audit) can support an additional review.

faqs.question: Should I use the exact wording from the advertisement?
faqs.answer: Use standard tool names and accurate professional terms. Do not copy sentences that describe work you have not done.

faqs.question: How many keywords does a CV need?
faqs.answer: There is no useful universal target. Cover the relevant capabilities you can support without making the document repetitive or misleading.

content: Matching a CV to a job description means making relevant evidence easier to find. It does not mean copying the advertisement into your experience section. The employer describes what the role needs. Your CV should explain which of those needs your background prepares you to address, with a clear distinction between direct experience and transferable skills.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Matching a CV to a job description means making relevant evidence easier to find. It does not mean copying the advertisement into your experience section.

The employer describes what the role needs. Your CV should explain which of those needs your background prepares you to address, with a clear distinction between direct experience and transferable skills.
Build a three-column match

Create columns for the requirement, your evidence and the best location in the CV. For “customer escalation handling,” your evidence might be resolving delayed-order complaints. For “team leadership,” it might be training colleagues rather than formally managing them.
That difference should remain visible. Do not convert informal training into a management title simply because the vacancy includes leadership responsibilities.
Choose the strongest examples

If several achievements support one requirement, select the most relevant and recent example. Avoid crowding the CV with repetitive bullets. A focused example is easier to assess than several generic claims.

For instance, an account manager applying to a service-led role might prioritise renewals and complaint resolution. For a sales-led role, the same person might emphasise pipeline development and verified revenue contribution. Their dates and core responsibilities do not change.
Edit the opening after the evidence

Once you know what supports the vacancy, revise the summary and skills section. The profile should introduce the experience already demonstrated below it. Writing it last can prevent an ambitious opening that the rest of the CV cannot support.

Use the employer's terminology where it accurately describes your work. If you have used a different system, name the real system and explain the relevant activity instead of silently replacing its name.
Remove empty repetition

Search the draft for repeated phrases. Ask whether each occurrence adds new information. A skill can appear in both the skills section and an experience example, but repeating it in every bullet usually reduces readability.
Never use white text or a pasted job description hidden at the end of the file. The document should be honest and useful to anyone who reads or extracts it.
Perform a final application check

Compare the CV against the essential requirements one more time. Check the cover letter, application answers and filename for references to another employer. Save the tailored version with enough detail to identify it later.

If you need help deciding which evidence to prioritise, bring the vacancy and your master CV to a [professional review](/services/packages/cv-review). The quality of the match depends on the facts available, not on reaching an arbitrary word count or score.

faqs.question: Can I use the same employment history for several roles?
faqs.answer: Yes. Keep the facts consistent while changing which relevant achievements you emphasise and how you introduce your experience.

faqs.question: What if I do not meet one requirement?
faqs.answer: Identify whether it is essential or preferred. Explain genuine transferable experience where appropriate, and do not claim a credential or skill you lack.

Combining them into one percentage can make the result appear more certain than it is.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: An ATS checker score can be a prompt for review, but it is not a universal grade that employers share. Always ask what the number actually measures.

A tool may assess text extraction, wording, formatting or similarity to a supplied job advertisement. Those are different questions. Combining them into one percentage can make the result appear more certain than it is.
Inspect the explanation behind the score

Look for specific findings you can verify. “Your email address was not detected” invites a practical check. “Your CV is weak” does not explain what to change. If the tool recommends a keyword, confirm that it is relevant and truthful before adding it.
Run the same reasoning in reverse: a high score does not establish that your achievements are accurate, that your professional level fits the role or that the employer will interview you.
Use the job description carefully

Some checkers compare your CV with the text you provide. A result based on a different vacancy may be irrelevant to the application you intend to send. A generic job description may also contain broad requirements that do not reflect the employer's priorities.
Review essential qualifications yourself. A tool's positive feedback should not override a missing mandatory credential or an application question you cannot answer truthfully.
Do not edit only to increase the number

Imagine a checker recommends “leadership” because the advertisement mentions it. If you trained two new colleagues, describe that work accurately. Adding “senior leader” to your headline would be an unsupported change, even if the score increases.

Keep a copy of the original draft and compare readability after edits. If sentences become crowded with repeated terms, reconsider the changes. Improving a measurement is useful only when the document also improves.
Consider privacy before uploading

A CV can contain personal contact information, employer details and sensitive achievements. Read the tool's data-handling information and use an appropriately redacted copy when testing an unfamiliar service.

Remove identity numbers, confidential customer information and unnecessary referee contact details. You should understand where your document is going before using a free score as an incentive to upload it.
Combine automated feedback with human judgment

Use a checker for observations, then review accuracy, relevance and clarity yourself. Ask another person to identify your strongest evidence without explanation. Their confusion can reveal a problem a numerical report misses.

The site's [ATS CV audit tool](/tools/ats-cv-audit) is a review aid. For feedback on positioning and writing, consider a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review). Neither is a promise of access to an employer's private screening process.

faqs.question: Is 80% a universal pass mark?
faqs.answer: No. A score belongs to the tool and method producing it. It does not define a shared threshold across employers.

faqs.question: Should I ignore checkers completely?
faqs.answer: No. Use clear, verifiable findings as suggestions. Reject changes that introduce inaccurate claims or make the CV harder to read.

author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Tables, icons and text boxes can create problems when they separate information that should be read together. Their presence alone does not prove a CV will fail.

The practical question is whether your finished document communicates the same career history visually and when its text is extracted. Review the specific layout rather than relying on an absolute rule about design elements.
Understand what can become disconnected

A table may place a role title in one cell and its dates in another. A text box may sit beside a paragraph visually while appearing elsewhere in the document's reading order. An icon may stand in for a label that a reader needs in words.

These issues matter most when they affect contact details, employment history or qualifications. Decorative elements that carry no essential information are a different concern from elements that contain your only email address.
Replace structure with simpler structure

Try writing each role as a short heading followed by employer, dates and bullets. Use normal paragraph spacing and alignment controls. Avoid using repeated spaces to imitate columns, because they can shift when fonts or viewers change.

For skills, replace a visual rating with a specific capability. “Prepared monthly Excel reconciliation worksheets” tells the reader what you did. Five coloured circles cannot explain the same experience.
Test before deciding

Copy all text from the exported file into a plain document. Read it without referring to the original. Check whether you can still associate each achievement with its role and each qualification with its institution.

Greenhouse's guidance identifies tables, headers and text boxes among formatting concerns that can affect parsing. That is a reason for caution, not evidence that all systems behave identically. See [the vendor's guidance](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200989175-Unsuccessful-resume-parse).
Preserve professional presentation

You can retain a polished appearance with consistent typography, spacing and restrained emphasis. If a visual layout is important for a creative application, consider linking to a portfolio while keeping the core career information straightforward.
Ask a second reader to review the simplified version. If it is easier to understand but looks too dense, adjust spacing and remove repetition before reintroducing complicated containers.
Check the actual upload
An employer's requested format takes priority. Review any extracted application fields and correct errors where possible. Keep the file you submitted so you can identify a problem later.
For document-specific help, send the editable file and final export to a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review). A screenshot alone cannot reveal the document's text structure.

faqs.question: Must every line or icon be removed?
faqs.answer: No. Focus on whether essential information remains written, connected and readable. Remove decoration that creates confusion or consumes needed space.

faqs.question: Is a table in Word always unsafe?
faqs.answer: No universal answer applies. Ordinary paragraphs are often easier to maintain, and extraction checks can reveal problems in your particular file.

content: The best CV font is one that remains clear in the final file. There is no magic typeface that guarantees an ATS pass or an interview. Choose typography to support reading, then check the export. A familiar font used at a comfortable size is usually a more practical choice than an unusual display font selected to make the document distinctive.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: The best CV font is one that remains clear in the final file. There is no magic typeface that guarantees an ATS pass or an interview.

Choose typography to support reading, then check the export. A familiar font used at a comfortable size is usually a more practical choice than an unusual display font selected to make the document distinctive.
Start with legibility

Arial, Calibri and Times New Roman are common options. The UK's National Careers Service recommends clear fonts and a size of at least 11 in its [CV guidance](https://nationalcareers.service.gov.uk/careers-advice/cv-sections). Treat that as a useful starting point rather than a universal employer specification.

Different fonts appear different sizes at the same point setting. Inspect the actual result, especially small numbers, punctuation and similar-looking characters. Your phone number and email should be easy to read without zooming excessively.
Establish a small type hierarchy

Use a larger size for your name, a clear heading style for sections and consistent body text. Bold role titles or employers selectively. Too many variations make the page harder to scan and harder to update.
Avoid using an ornate font for essential information. If you want a distinctive visual identity, restrained colour and spacing can provide it without making the words difficult to interpret.
Do not solve length by shrinking everything
If the CV spills onto another page, remove repetition and irrelevant detail first. Combine overlapping bullets, shorten an overlong summary and reduce detail in older roles where appropriate.
Tiny text may technically fit more information, but it transfers the editing problem to the reader. A concise document should be selective, not merely compressed.
Check font behaviour after export
Open the final file on another viewer or device if possible. Look for changed line breaks, missing characters and substituted fonts. Test links and check whether long headings still fit.
When applying through a portal, use the requested file type and review its preview. The document that reaches the employer matters more than the version that looked correct in your editor.
Keep the content in perspective

A font choice will not repair vague achievements or an unclear target role. Once the document is readable, spend most of your editing time on accurate, relevant evidence. Ask someone to identify what you offer before asking which font they prefer.
Explore [free CV resources](/resources) for a starting structure or request a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) when you need feedback on both presentation and writing.

faqs.question: Is Calibri better than Arial for ATS?
faqs.answer: There is no universal hiring advantage from that choice alone. Use a clear font consistently and verify the actual exported file.

faqs.question: Can I use two fonts?
faqs.answer: Yes, if both are readable and the hierarchy is consistent. One font is simply easier to maintain and usually sufficient.

content: Use the file type the employer requests. When both PDF and Word are accepted, choose a clean, text-based document and inspect the final version before uploading. Neither extension guarantees a readable CV. A scanned PDF can behave very differently from a text-based PDF, while a Word document can contain complicated objects and unstable page layouts.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Use the file type the employer requests. When both PDF and Word are accepted, choose a clean, text-based document and inspect the final version before uploading.
Neither extension guarantees a readable CV. A scanned PDF can behave very differently from a text-based PDF, while a Word document can contain complicated objects and unstable page layouts.
Follow the application instructions first

Check the vacancy, upload field and any recruiter message for accepted formats and size limits. Do not send your preferred type if the employer explicitly asks for another. If instructions conflict, seek clarification where practical rather than guessing.
Keep an editable master so you can produce another version without rebuilding the CV. Save the final application file separately from your working draft.
Review a PDF as a finished document

A PDF is useful for presenting a fixed layout. Open every page after export and check that text is selectable, links work and nothing has been clipped. Copy a section into a plain document to inspect the reading order.
Do not assume that a PDF made from photographs or screenshots contains useful text. If all you have is an image, rebuild the CV in an editable document before exporting a proper application version.
Review a Word file for editing artefacts
Check for comments, tracked changes, highlighted instructions and accidental blank pages. Make sure another reader will not see unresolved edits or an earlier version of a sentence.

Use consistent styles and sensible page breaks. A document that depends on many spaces, floating text boxes or unusual fonts may shift when opened elsewhere. Preview it in another available viewer if you can.
Verify what the portal received

After upload, inspect any document preview and automatically populated fields. Correct extraction mistakes where allowed. Confirm that the file attached is the right version for the employer and role.
Use a filename that identifies you and the document without clutter, such as your name and target role. Avoid filenames that expose internal notes or suggest the file is an unfinished draft.
Make a reusable submission routine
Keep the editable master, an exported version and a record of which file you submitted. Repeat the check after substantial edits, because a new bullet can create an awkward page break.

If you request [CV writing support](/services/packages/cv-writing), confirm the supplied formats in advance. A [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) should examine the final export as well as the wording when file usability is your concern.

faqs.question: Should I always send PDF?
faqs.answer: No. Follow the employer's instructions. If a recruiter specifically requests Word, provide a clean Word version.

faqs.question: Does changing the extension convert a file?
faqs.answer: No. Export or save the document using the appropriate format in your editor. Renaming an extension does not change the underlying file.

author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: An application system may extract information from your CV, store the original file and make candidate details available to recruiters. The exact workflow varies by employer.
Understanding those separate functions helps you prepare a clearer application. It also prevents the mistaken idea that every ATS reads every CV in the same way and returns one universal score.
Think in terms of fields and relationships
Your CV contains connected facts: a role belongs to an employer, dates describe that role and achievements explain work performed there. A clear document makes these relationships visible.

If employer names and dates are scattered across a complicated layout, interpretation can become harder. Use a consistent sequence and familiar headings so the professional history is understandable even without decorative formatting.
Distinguish the extracted data from the original file
A recruiter may have access to both a document and information entered into the application system. Those views can differ if extraction is incomplete or if you type a different answer into the form.

Check any auto-filled fields before submission. Do not assume that uploading the CV means every field is correct. Equally, do not assume that an extraction error automatically prevents anyone from seeing the original attachment.
Make terminology understandable

Use recognisable names for tools, qualifications and activities. Explain internal abbreviations when an outside reader would not know them. Keep official job titles intact and add a truthful functional clarification if necessary.

For example, “Customer Service Executive — order support and complaint handling” provides useful context if those activities reflect the role. Replacing the title with “Customer Success Manager” would require a factual basis, not just keyword preference.
Answer screening questions independently

Application questions may request information that is not obvious in the CV. Read and answer them accurately. Do not rely on a sentence in the attachment when the employer has specifically asked for a separate response.

If a field has a character limit, prioritise the requested evidence rather than pasting a whole experience section. Save a copy of substantive answers when appropriate so you can prepare consistently for later stages.
Test what you control
Open the final file, copy its text into a plain document and check the order. Inspect links and dates. Then review the portal's preview and populated fields before submitting.

These are practical quality checks, not access to the employer's internal settings. Use the [ATS CV audit tool](/tools/ats-cv-audit) as supplementary feedback and a [professional review](/services/packages/cv-review) for document-specific advice.

faqs.question: Can I know exactly how an employer's ATS ranks applicants?
faqs.answer: Usually not from the outside. Public advice and checker scores do not reveal a private employer's complete configuration or hiring process.

faqs.question: Should I fill application fields when the same information is in my CV?
faqs.answer: Yes, when requested. Keep the information consistent and correct any automatically imported errors before submission.

content: A professional CV can look polished through careful typography, spacing and editing. It does not need elaborate graphics to communicate quality. For job seekers in Sri Lanka, the useful design goal is a document that feels organised and makes relevant evidence easy to find. Start with content hierarchy, then use visual choices to support it.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: A professional CV can look polished through careful typography, spacing and editing. It does not need elaborate graphics to communicate quality.
For job seekers in Sri Lanka, the useful design goal is a document that feels organised and makes relevant evidence easy to find. Start with content hierarchy, then use visual choices to support it.
Build the page around the reader's questions

The opening should identify your professional direction. The next sections should show the experience, skills and qualifications that support it. Keep the most relevant evidence prominent without hiding the chronology.
A strong layout gives each section a clear purpose. An oversized name, long generic summary or decorative sidebar can consume space that would be better used for achievements.
Use a restrained visual system

Choose one readable body font, consistent headings and predictable spacing. Use bold text to distinguish role titles or employers. A subtle accent colour can help navigation, but the document should remain readable when printed without colour.
Avoid extremely pale text. Secondary information such as dates still needs to be legible. Decorative elements should never be the only way a reader identifies a skill or contact method.
Let writing create the premium impression

Specific, well-edited experience often looks more professional than a busy design. Compare “hardworking team player” with a clear example of coordinating a handover or resolving a recurring reporting issue.

Keep bullets concise enough to scan while preserving the context and your contribution. Remove repetition before reducing font size. Consistent sentence structure makes the page calmer without making every achievement sound identical.
Separate the CV from the portfolio
If your work is visual, link to a portfolio with selected projects and short explanations. The CV can describe your role and results, while the portfolio demonstrates the work itself.

Check access permissions and remove confidential client material. A link to a portfolio that requires unexpected sign-in or contains unexplained screenshots can weaken an otherwise polished application.
Verify function before calling it finished

Open the exported file, check all pages and test links. Copy the text into a plain document and inspect the reading order. Ask someone to find your latest role and strongest relevant achievement quickly.

If the page is beautiful but those tasks are difficult, revise the hierarchy. If it is readable but crowded, simplify the wording and spacing. The [CV writing service](/services/packages/cv-writing) can help balance content and presentation, while [CV reviews](/services/packages/cv-review) offer focused feedback on an existing draft.

faqs.question: Can I use colour on an ATS-friendly CV?
faqs.answer: Yes, when it remains readable and does not carry essential information alone. Strong contrast and restrained use are practical defaults.

faqs.question: Do I need a designer for a premium-looking CV?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Good writing, consistent styles and careful export checks can produce a professional document using a simple template.

Do not interpret a completed checklist as a guaranteed interview. Its purpose is to catch avoidable errors before the employer receives your file.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Use this twenty-point checklist on the exact CV you plan to submit. It covers accuracy, relevance, document usability and the application itself.
Do not interpret a completed checklist as a guaranteed interview. Its purpose is to catch avoidable errors before the employer receives your file.
Confirm the facts

items: Your name is written consistently across application materials.
Your phone number includes an appropriate country code for overseas contact.
Your email address is current and typed correctly.
Employment titles and dates match your actual history.
Qualifications clearly distinguish completed and ongoing study.

body.text: Correct factual errors before adjusting wording. A polished summary does not compensate for a missing digit in a phone number or an inaccurate qualification claim.
Check relevance

items: The opening identifies the role or professional direction you are targeting.
Essential requirements have been reviewed for genuine eligibility.
Relevant tools and responsibilities use accurate, recognisable terms.
Recent experience includes specific evidence of your contribution.
Unsupported claims and invented numerical results have been removed.

body.text: Keep a note of where each major achievement came from. You should be able to explain the context and your role if an interviewer asks.
Inspect the document

items: Section headings clearly identify experience, education and skills.
Employers, titles and dates remain connected in the reading order.
Important details appear as text rather than only images or icons.
The exported file opens without missing text or clipped content.
Portfolio and LinkedIn links lead to the intended pages.

body.text: A text-copy check can reveal scrambled information, while a visual review catches awkward spacing and page breaks. Use both rather than assuming one proves everything.
Complete the application carefully

items: The file type matches the employer's instructions.
The file meets any stated upload-size limit.
Automatically populated fields have been reviewed and corrected where possible.
Required statements, forms and cover letters are included.
The filename and saved version identify the correct application.

body.text: Turn the checklist into a routine

Create a small application folder containing the vacancy, submitted CV and any substantive answers. Record the submission date and confirmation. This makes follow-up and interview preparation easier without repeatedly reconstructing what you sent.

When a check fails, fix the underlying issue. Do not simply hide an unsupported claim or rename a file to imitate a requested format. If several problems involve unclear writing, a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) can help prioritise the work. The [ATS audit tool](/tools/ats-cv-audit) can provide additional observations, but your factual review remains essential.

faqs.question: Should I repeat the checklist for every vacancy?
faqs.answer: Repeat the application-specific checks each time and the full document checks after meaningful edits or a new export.

faqs.question: Does the checklist replace tailoring?
faqs.answer: No. It helps verify a tailored application. You still need to select evidence that is relevant to the particular role.

content: Keywords identify relevant subjects, but they do not demonstrate ability. A recruiter still needs to understand what you did, where you did it and why it mattered. Copying an advertisement can make a CV look superficially aligned while leaving the evidence weak. Use the employer's requirements to guide your selection of real examples instead.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Keywords identify relevant subjects, but they do not demonstrate ability. A recruiter still needs to understand what you did, where you did it and why it mattered.
Copying an advertisement can make a CV look superficially aligned while leaving the evidence weak. Use the employer's requirements to guide your selection of real examples instead.
Translate a requirement into a question

If the advert asks for stakeholder management, ask yourself which stakeholders you worked with, what you needed to coordinate and what decisions or outcomes followed. If it asks for reporting, identify the reports, audience, tools and purpose.
This process uncovers usable evidence. Simply inserting “stakeholder management” into the skills section leaves all those questions unanswered.
Distinguish knowledge from application
You may have studied a method, used it in a university project or applied it professionally. Those are all possible forms of evidence, but they should be labelled accurately.

For example, a student can describe a SQL project and the queries they wrote. They should not imply responsibility for a production database if the work was a classroom exercise. Accurate scope is more credible than inflated terminology.
Write one concrete example

Consider the requirement “process improvement.” A useful bullet might explain that you introduced a shared request tracker and defined handover responsibilities. If you have reliable evidence of a result, add it. If not, describe the implemented change without inventing a percentage.
The keyword can still appear, but it now has a factual foundation. The reader can ask meaningful follow-up questions about the work.
Keep gaps visible to yourself

Create a private list of requirements you cannot yet support. Some may be preferred rather than essential; others may indicate that a different role is a better target. Use the list to plan learning or identify suitable projects.
Do not hide a real gap by borrowing wording from someone else's CV. An application should present your strongest relevant case, not simulate a background you do not have.
Review the complete story
Read your summary, skills and experience together. Does each important claim lead to an example? Are you using terminology consistently? Could you explain the work in your own words at an interview?

If the answer is no, improve the evidence before adding more keywords. A [professional CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) can help identify unsupported claims and missed examples. For a full rewrite, explore [CV writing packages](/services/packages/cv-writing) and provide real information about your contribution.

faqs.question: Should I avoid words from the job advertisement?
faqs.answer: No. Accurate professional terminology is useful. The problem is copying requirements without evidence that they describe your background.

faqs.question: Can transferable skills count as evidence?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the connection is explained honestly. Describe the original context and show how the skill relates to the new role.
