author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Tailoring a CV is faster when you maintain a complete master record and change only the emphasis needed for each vacancy. Your factual history should remain consistent.
The aim is not to produce a new professional identity for every application. It is to help each employer find the evidence most relevant to its role.
Build a master evidence bank

Keep accurate titles, dates, responsibilities, projects and achievements in one private document. Include notes about results and where the information can be verified. This master can be longer than an application CV because it is a source record, not a submission.
Group achievements by themes such as customer service, analysis, coordination or leadership. That makes it easier to find relevant examples without searching through old application files.
Identify the vacancy's main priorities

Read essential requirements and responsibilities. Select the few priorities that define the role, then match them to your strongest evidence. Do not treat every word in a long advertisement as equally important.
If your evidence is weak for an essential requirement, consider whether the application is suitable. Tailoring cannot turn a missing qualification into a completed one.
Edit a small set of areas

items: Adjust the summary to introduce the relevant career direction.
Reorder the skills section around genuine role requirements.
Select or reorder achievements within recent roles.
Choose projects that demonstrate the required capabilities.
Remove detail that distracts from the application.

body.text: Keep employers, official titles, dates and qualification status unchanged. Do not move dates or alter seniority to make the match look stronger.
Use role-family versions carefully

If you regularly apply for closely related roles, maintain a small number of base versions. An operations-focused CV and a customer-success-focused CV might draw from the same history but prioritise different evidence.
Review each against the actual vacancy before sending. A base version is a starting point, not permission to skip reading the advertisement.
Finish with a consistency check

Compare the CV with your cover letter and application answers. Search for another employer's name, stale role titles and old filenames. Open the export and save the exact submitted version with the vacancy.

This routine makes later interview preparation easier: you can revisit the examples the employer has already seen. If your master CV needs restructuring, [professional writing support](/services/packages/cv-writing) can help build a maintainable foundation. A [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) may be enough if your content is already strong.

faqs.question: Must I rewrite every bullet for every job?
faqs.answer: No. Keep strong relevant evidence and change its emphasis where needed. Many factual sections can remain identical across related applications.

faqs.question: How many CV versions should I keep?
faqs.answer: Keep as few base versions as you can manage reliably, plus records of actual submissions. Avoid a large collection of inconsistent drafts.

For example, explain that you coordinated customer orders across two internal teams, then describe a specific handover improvement you introduced. Do not attribute a whole department's results to yourself without explaining your role.
Keep progression visible

Use distinct titles and dates for promotions. Explain increased responsibility through the work itself: larger scope, greater independence, more complex decisions or formal supervision. Repeating identical duties under every role makes progression difficult to assess.
Shorter early-career entries can preserve the chronology without competing with recent relevant work. Do not erase older experience if doing so creates a misleading history.
Anticipate questions about credibility

An interviewer may ask how you calculated a result, which tools you used or what you personally delivered. Review every major claim before submitting. If a bullet was professionally written, make sure you still recognise and understand the work it describes.
Check consistency with LinkedIn and the application form. Different wording is fine; incompatible titles, dates or qualification claims require correction.
Make the next step easy

Provide current contact details and functioning links. If a portfolio is relevant, select a few accessible examples with clear explanations. Do not make the reader request permission simply to understand the work you chose to showcase.

Use a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) to assess the full reading experience. The [ATS audit tool](/tools/ats-cv-audit) can supplement that review, but a numerical result cannot replace judgment about relevance and credibility.

faqs.question: Does an ATS-friendly CV guarantee that a recruiter reads it?
faqs.answer: No. Application volume, eligibility, timing and the employer's workflow all affect what happens next.

faqs.question: Should I write only for the recruiter and ignore software?
faqs.answer: Prepare for both. Use a readable file and clear terminology while making the career story useful to a person.

content: A useful CV must be easy to process and worth reading. ATS optimisation and recruiter-focused writing address different parts of that requirement. The first concerns accessible information and accurate terminology. The second concerns relevance, evidence and interpretation. Treat them as complementary checks rather than competing approaches.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: A useful CV must be easy to process and worth reading. ATS optimisation and recruiter-focused writing address different parts of that requirement.
The first concerns accessible information and accurate terminology. The second concerns relevance, evidence and interpretation. Treat them as complementary checks rather than competing approaches.
Start with a factual foundation

Gather correct dates, titles, qualifications and achievements. Identify the target role and match its requirements to your background. Without that foundation, formatting changes and keyword edits can make the document look stronger without making it more accurate.
Keep a separate record of supporting details so you can explain results and scope. Do not publish confidential evidence merely to make a claim appear more impressive.
Perform a document-readability pass

Check section headings, contact details and the relationship between employers, roles and dates. Open the final file and inspect the reading order by copying text into a plain document. Follow upload instructions and check automatically populated fields.
This pass addresses usability. It does not establish that the candidate is qualified or that the document tells a compelling career story.
Perform a recruiter-reading pass

Ask whether the opening identifies your professional direction. Check that relevant achievements are easy to locate and that the reader can distinguish your contribution from routine responsibilities.

An operations candidate might list inventory management as a skill. The recruiter-focused version also explains the actual work: reconciling stock records, investigating discrepancies and coordinating replenishment. The keyword becomes useful because it is connected to evidence.
Resolve conflicts through clarity

If a keyword makes a sentence awkward, rewrite the sentence rather than repeating the word elsewhere. If a design hides important content, simplify the layout rather than creating a hidden text version.
Similarly, do not remove essential context just to make a document shorter. Edit repetition first, then decide which information the specific application needs.
Use two separate review questions

The technical question is, “Can the information be read and associated correctly?” The editorial question is, “Does this information explain why I am relevant?” A strong CV needs sensible answers to both.

Ask another person to review the exported document without explanation. Their questions can reveal missing context, while an extraction check can reveal structural problems. Use [CV writing services](/services/packages/cv-writing) if both content and structure need work, or a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) for focused feedback.

faqs.question: Which should I optimise first?
faqs.answer: Begin with accurate, relevant content. Then make the structure readable and review the final file from both technical and human perspectives.

faqs.question: Can one simple CV satisfy both needs?
faqs.answer: Yes. Clear headings, specific achievements, accurate terminology and consistent formatting can support software processing and human review together.

content: Write a professional CV by choosing a target role, collecting accurate evidence and organising it for the employer who will read it. Formatting comes after those decisions. This sequence works for a first draft or a substantial update. Keep a complete private record of your background, then create a focused application document from it.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha
keywords: how to write a CV Sri Lanka

body.text: Write a professional CV by choosing a target role, collecting accurate evidence and organising it for the employer who will read it. Formatting comes after those decisions.
This sequence works for a first draft or a substantial update. Keep a complete private record of your background, then create a focused application document from it.
Step 1: Define the application

Read a representative vacancy. Identify essential qualifications, main responsibilities and relevant tools. Write down which requirements you can support directly and which need a careful explanation of transferable experience.
Do not begin with a template that decides your priorities for you. A student may need prominent projects; an experienced professional may need recent achievements first.
Step 2: Gather the facts

Collect employment dates, official titles, qualification names and relevant project details. For each role, record what you did, the scope and any result you can verify. Distinguish individual contributions from team achievements.
Use this stage to resolve uncertain dates or numerical claims. It is easier to correct the source information now than after several application versions exist.
Step 3: Draft the evidence sections

Write recent experience and projects before the summary. Use specific actions and explain their purpose. “Prepared reports” could become “prepared weekly order-status reports for the operations team, highlighting unresolved delivery issues.”
Include education and certifications with accurate completion status. Select skills you can demonstrate rather than filling space with generic personal qualities.
Step 4: Write the opening

Summarise your professional direction, relevant strengths and supporting context in a few clear lines. The profile should introduce what the document actually proves. Avoid claiming seniority or expertise beyond your background.
Step 5: Format and verify

Use readable text, consistent dates and familiar headings. Open the exported file, check all pages and test links. Compare the CV with the application form and LinkedIn. Ask someone to identify your strongest relevant evidence without additional explanation.

Save a master and a separate copy of each submission. Update the master after meaningful projects or promotions so the next application is easier. For support, explore [CV writing packages](/services/packages/cv-writing) or begin with a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review).

faqs.question: Should I include every job?
faqs.answer: Preserve an accurate career history, but adjust the detail according to relevance. Older roles may need only brief entries.

faqs.question: Can I write a strong CV myself?
faqs.answer: Yes. Clear evidence, careful editing and useful feedback matter more than purchasing a particular template or service.

title: The Perfect CV Structure for Sri Lankan Job Seekers
excerpt: There is no perfect structure for every Sri Lankan CV. The best order brings relevant evidence forward while keeping your background easy to follow. Start with the…
content: There is no perfect structure for every Sri Lankan CV. The best order brings relevant evidence forward while keeping your background easy to follow. Start with the employer's requirements and your career stage. Use the structures below as adaptable starting points, not rigid rules that override application instructions.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: There is no perfect structure for every Sri Lankan CV. The best order brings relevant evidence forward while keeping your background easy to follow.
Start with the employer's requirements and your career stage. Use the structures below as adaptable starting points, not rigid rules that override application instructions.
A structure for experienced professionals

Begin with your name and contact details, followed by a concise professional summary, relevant skills, experience, education and certifications. Put recent roles first and keep each employer, title and date range together.

Use a brief scope statement if the role needs context, then selected achievements. Avoid separating all achievements from the roles where they occurred; the reader should be able to understand when and where you delivered them.
A structure for students and graduates

Education and projects may deserve space before a short work history. Include internships, volunteering or university leadership when they demonstrate relevant skills. Label these experiences accurately rather than presenting everything as paid employment.

For a software internship, a well-explained project may be stronger evidence than an unrelated short job. For customer-service work, that job may be highly relevant. The vacancy determines the emphasis.
A structure for career changes
Use the opening to explain the new direction and identify transferable strengths. Include relevant training or projects prominently, while retaining a clear employment chronology.
Avoid using a skills-only layout to hide your history. A reader should be able to understand both the transition and the actual experience supporting it.
Make each section earn its space

Ask what question every section answers. Skills identify capabilities; experience provides evidence; education establishes qualifications. A long objective repeating the summary adds little. A separate list of generic strengths may duplicate both.

Keep contact details practical. Include a professional email, phone number and relevant profile or portfolio links. Consider whether any additional personal information is actually needed for the application.
Test the order with a reader
Ask someone to find your current role, strongest relevant achievement and key qualification. If these are difficult to locate, adjust the hierarchy before changing the visual design.
The [career resources](/resources) offer starting materials, and a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) can help determine which structure best supports your target role.

faqs.question: Must education always come first?
faqs.answer: No. It may lead for students, while relevant professional experience usually deserves greater prominence as your career develops.

faqs.question: Should I use a different structure for every job?
faqs.answer: Usually only the emphasis changes. Keep a stable, readable structure unless the application requires a substantially different document.

content: A CV should be long enough to present the relevant evidence clearly and short enough to avoid unnecessary repetition. Page count is a constraint, not the purpose. Follow an employer's explicit limit first. Without one, decide according to your career stage, the role and the amount of evidence the reader needs.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha
keywords: how long should a CV be

body.text: A CV should be long enough to present the relevant evidence clearly and short enough to avoid unnecessary repetition. Page count is a constraint, not the purpose.
Follow an employer's explicit limit first. Without one, decide according to your career stage, the role and the amount of evidence the reader needs.
When one page can work

A student or early-career applicant may be able to present education, a few projects and limited experience on one readable page. That works when nothing important is omitted and the text remains comfortable to read.
Do not add filler to reach a second page. Equally, do not remove the explanation of your strongest project simply because an online rule says all first CVs must be one page.
When two pages can help

Several relevant roles, technical projects or leadership achievements may need more space. A second page is useful when it adds evidence, not when it repeats the summary or lists every routine responsibility.
Keep the first page strong. The opening and recent relevant experience should establish your fit, while the remaining space supports that impression with qualifications and additional evidence.
Recognise specialist exceptions

Academic, research and some specialist applications can require detailed records or additional documents. Read their instructions rather than forcing publications, teaching and projects into a commercial CV format.
If an employer requests separate statements or selection-criteria answers, prepare those separately. Do not assume that extra CV pages can replace a required response.
Edit content before shrinking text
Remove duplicated duties, generic objectives and irrelevant detail. Reduce older roles to their necessary context. Combine overlapping bullets without losing your contribution or the result.
Then inspect spacing and page breaks. A page containing only a few lines may indicate a layout issue, while dense tiny text indicates that you have compressed too aggressively.
Use a relevance test

For every paragraph, ask whether it helps assess suitability for this vacancy. Keep valuable evidence and cut content that does not. Ask a reader which parts feel repetitive or difficult to understand.
A [professional CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) can help make those choices. The goal should be a clearer application, not achieving a page count for its own sake.

faqs.question: Is a two-page CV too long for a graduate?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Relevant projects and internships may justify it, but one clear page is preferable to two pages of filler.

faqs.question: Should senior professionals always use three pages?
faqs.answer: No. Seniority does not determine a fixed length. Follow the application instructions and include the evidence needed to communicate scope and impact.

content: A professional summary should help the reader interpret your CV. It identifies your career direction and strongest relevant capabilities before the detailed evidence begins. Avoid treating it as a place for ambitious adjectives. “Dynamic, hardworking and passionate” can describe almost anyone. Specific context makes the opening useful.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: A professional summary should help the reader interpret your CV. It identifies your career direction and strongest relevant capabilities before the detailed evidence begins.
Avoid treating it as a place for ambitious adjectives. “Dynamic, hardworking and passionate” can describe almost anyone. Specific context makes the opening useful.
Write the summary after the evidence

Draft your experience and projects first. Identify the themes they support, then write the opening around those themes. This prevents claiming expertise that the rest of the document does not demonstrate.
Decide which role the CV targets. If you are applying for both marketing and operations work, the same opening may not give either employer a clear reason to continue.
Use four ingredients

items: Your actual professional identity or career stage.
Two or three capabilities that matter to the target role.
A credible indication of the work or value you can contribute.

body.text: You do not need a sentence for every ingredient. Keep the paragraph concise and avoid listing every skill you have ever used.
Compare a vague and a specific opening
Vague: “A motivated individual seeking a challenging position in a reputed organisation where I can use my skills.”

Illustrative alternative: “Customer-service professional experienced in order coordination, complaint resolution and daily service reporting. Comfortable working with sales and operations teams to track unresolved requests and keep customers informed.”
The alternative supplies context without inventing revenue figures or claiming an unrealistic outcome. Adapt the structure to your real experience rather than copying the example as a personal claim.
Handle a career change honestly

Name the transferable foundation and relevant preparation. A teacher moving toward learning and development might emphasise training design, learner assessment and recent workplace-learning study. They should not call themselves an experienced corporate L&D manager without that background.
Remove claims that add little

Check each adjective and ask what evidence supports it. Replace broad claims with specific strengths where possible. Avoid “expert” if your experience is introductory, and do not add years of experience without checking the relevant timeline.

Read the summary beside the vacancy and your first experience entry. All three should connect. For help clarifying the opening, explore [CV writing](/services/packages/cv-writing) or request a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review).

faqs.question: How long should the summary be?
faqs.answer: A few focused lines are a useful starting point. The goal is an accurate introduction, not a second cover letter.

faqs.question: Can a graduate write a professional summary?
faqs.answer: Yes. State your degree or career direction, relevant projects and demonstrated capabilities without pretending to have years of professional experience.

title: Stop Listing Job Duties: Write Achievement-Based CV Bullet Points Instead
excerpt: Achievement-based CV bullets explain your contribution rather than merely repeating the job description. They help an employer understand what you did with your…
content: Achievement-based CV bullets explain your contribution rather than merely repeating the job description. They help an employer understand what you did with your responsibilities. Not every bullet needs a percentage. Specific scope, a completed improvement or a clear deliverable can provide useful evidence when reliable numerical results are unavailable.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Achievement-based CV bullets explain your contribution rather than merely repeating the job description. They help an employer understand what you did with your responsibilities.
Not every bullet needs a percentage. Specific scope, a completed improvement or a clear deliverable can provide useful evidence when reliable numerical results are unavailable.
Begin with a real piece of work

Choose a task, project or problem you remember clearly. Write what the situation required, what you personally did and what happened next. Keep supporting details in private notes so you can discuss the example later.
Do not begin by searching for an impressive verb. The action becomes clearer once the underlying contribution is understood.
Use action, context and outcome
Duty: “Responsible for monthly reporting.”
Illustrative improvement: “Prepared monthly branch-performance reports, checked inconsistent entries and summarised unresolved issues for the finance team.”

If there is a verified result, add it. If not, the improved version still identifies the output, activity and audience. Avoid attaching a made-up time-saving percentage simply to make the bullet look achievement-focused.
Choose evidence appropriate to the role

A customer-service bullet may discuss resolving an escalation or improving a handover. An engineering bullet may describe a technical deliverable and validation. A manager's bullet may explain a decision and the team or budget scope involved.
The relevant evidence depends on what the next employer needs. A technically impressive achievement may deserve less space if it is unrelated to the target role.
Keep ownership accurate

Use “supported,” “coordinated,” “developed” or “led” according to your actual contribution. If a result came from a team, explain the part you owned. Do not present a company-wide improvement as your individual achievement without justification.
Confidential results can be described at an appropriate level of detail. Do not disclose customer names or private business data just to make a bullet more specific.
Edit for readability
Keep one main idea per bullet. Remove introductory phrases such as “duties included being responsible for.” Check that a reader unfamiliar with your company can understand the terminology.

Read your strongest bullets aloud and prepare a short explanation of each. A [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) can help identify vague claims and missing context; [professional writing](/services/packages/cv-writing) can help reorganise a duty-heavy document.

faqs.question: Does every bullet need a measurable result?
faqs.answer: No. Accurate scope, a delivered output or a documented improvement can be useful evidence without a numerical claim.

faqs.question: Can routine work be an achievement?
faqs.answer: Yes, when you explain the contribution, complexity or improvement. Do not exaggerate routine work, but do not assume it has no value.

title: How to Turn Ordinary Job Responsibilities Into Powerful CV Achievements
excerpt: Ordinary responsibilities often contain evidence you have stopped noticing. To find it, examine a specific piece of work rather than trying to make a duty sound grander.…
content: Ordinary responsibilities often contain evidence you have stopped noticing. To find it, examine a specific piece of work rather than trying to make a duty sound grander. This method helps when your CV currently says only “handled customers,” “managed documents” or “supported operations.” The aim is to uncover facts, not invent impact.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Ordinary responsibilities often contain evidence you have stopped noticing. To find it, examine a specific piece of work rather than trying to make a duty sound grander.
This method helps when your CV currently says only “handled customers,” “managed documents” or “supported operations.” The aim is to uncover facts, not invent impact.
Ask what made the work necessary
Why did the task exist? Who depended on it? What could go wrong if it was not completed properly? These questions reveal context that a basic duty statement omits.
For document handling, the useful context might be maintaining complete files for an internal review. For customer support, it might be resolving missing-order information across several teams.
Identify your actual decisions
Record what you checked, changed, organised or clarified. Did you create a tracker, investigate an inconsistency, coordinate a handover or explain a process to colleagues?

An illustrative rewrite could be: “Maintained a document checklist and followed up on missing records before scheduled internal reviews.” That is more informative than “handled files” without claiming a result that has not been measured.
Look for evidence of scope or result

Useful evidence may include the number of locations supported, the reporting frequency, the type of customer issue or a completed deliverable. Use figures only when they are accurate and appropriate to disclose.

If you describe improvement, establish what changed. A new process being introduced is not automatically proof of reduced errors. State the implementation clearly and add an outcome only when you have a sound basis.
Select achievements for the next role
Keep a private evidence bank with more examples than the CV needs. Choose the ones most relevant to the vacancy. This avoids crowding the document with every small improvement you have ever made.
A candidate moving into coordination work may prioritise scheduling and follow-up examples. The same candidate targeting analysis may emphasise investigation and reporting.
Check the finished wording
Ask whether you can explain the example naturally in an interview. Remove inflated verbs or unfamiliar claims introduced during editing. Keep team ownership and your individual contribution distinct.

If you struggle to recognise useful evidence, a [CV writing consultation through the service](/services/packages/cv-writing) can help organise the questions. Bring notes about real work rather than expecting a writer to create achievements from a job title alone.

faqs.question: What if my employer did not track results?
faqs.answer: Describe verified activities, scope and deliverables. Do not invent a percentage; explain what you changed or completed and why it mattered.

faqs.question: Should I include small improvements?
faqs.answer: Include them when they demonstrate skills relevant to the target role. Relevance and clarity matter more than making every example sound large.

title: The Skills Section Most CVs Get Completely Wrong

content: A skills section should help employers identify relevant capabilities. A long list of generic qualities or every tool you have encountered makes that task harder. Start with the target role and select skills you can demonstrate. The section is a concise index to your evidence, not a substitute for experience or projects.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: A skills section should help employers identify relevant capabilities. A long list of generic qualities or every tool you have encountered makes that task harder.
Start with the target role and select skills you can demonstrate. The section is a concise index to your evidence, not a substitute for experience or projects.
Separate capability from personality claims

Communication and teamwork can matter, but almost anyone can list them. Show those qualities through a relevant example, such as explaining reports to a nontechnical audience or coordinating a cross-team handover.

Use the skills section for clearer professional terms where appropriate: financial reporting, inventory reconciliation, SQL, campaign analysis or training coordination. Select only those that accurately describe your background.
Group skills for the reader

An IT applicant might group languages, tools and methods. A finance applicant might separate accounting activities from systems. A general operations applicant may only need a short, well-ordered list.
Avoid overcomplicating the grouping. The reader should not need to understand your personal classification system before finding an essential skill.
Describe proficiency honestly

Stars and percentages rarely explain ability. “Excel: pivot tables and reconciliation workbooks” is clearer than “Excel: 85%.” A student learning Python can label it as project experience instead of implying advanced professional use.
Do not list a tool merely because it appears in the vacancy. If you have used a related tool, name the real one and explain transferable work in the experience section.
Connect skills to examples
Check your most important skills against the rest of the CV. Where did you use each one? What did you produce? Could you answer an interview question about it?
If a central skill appears nowhere else, either add accurate evidence or reconsider its prominence. A course can support learning, but course completion alone does not prove extensive application.
Keep the list current

Remove obsolete or irrelevant tools when they distract from the target role. Add new skills after meaningful use, not simply after seeing a tutorial. Review the order for each application without changing the underlying facts.

Use a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) for feedback on skills and evidence. For a broader rewrite, explore [CV writing services](/services/packages/cv-writing) and bring examples of the work behind each capability.

faqs.question: Should I remove all soft skills?
faqs.answer: No. Demonstrate important interpersonal skills through specific work examples, and use the skills list selectively when a term is relevant.

faqs.question: Is a longer skills section better?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. A focused, credible list is easier to assess than a large collection of weakly supported keywords.

author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Do not add a CV photo automatically because a template includes one. Consider the employer's instructions, the role and the country where you are applying.
For an ordinary application without a photo requirement, a text-focused CV is a sensible starting point. Your qualifications and evidence should remain the main basis of the document.
Read the request carefully

An employer may request a photo through a separate application form or specialist portfolio. That does not necessarily mean a large portrait belongs on the CV itself. Follow the specific instructions and verify that the request comes from the genuine employer.
If there is no instruction, consider whether the image adds useful professional information. For most office roles, space is often better used for achievements, skills or projects.
Distinguish a CV from a professional profile
A LinkedIn profile and a job-application document serve different purposes. Choosing to use a professional profile photograph does not create a requirement to put the same image on every CV.

Likewise, a portfolio may require visual presentation relevant to the profession. Keep any requested visual material in the appropriate format instead of assuming that every career document should look identical.
Consider the destination market

Application conventions vary. Canada's Job Bank states that a photo is not the norm on Canadian resumes; see its [resume guidance](https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/findajob/resources/write-good-resume?wbdisable=true). Do not export a familiar local template without reviewing the target employer's expectations.
This is practical document guidance, not a claim that one rule applies to every profession or country. Employer instructions and specialist requirements may differ.
If a photo is genuinely required

Use an appropriate, current image and keep the document readable. Avoid heavy filters, distracting backgrounds or a photo so large that it displaces essential career evidence. Do not include unrelated personal images.
Check the final file size and the quality of the export. The addition should not turn the entire CV into an image or make the text difficult to select.
Make a deliberate decision

Keep a clean version without a photo so you can adapt quickly. Review the request for each application rather than maintaining one design for every market. For support with target-market presentation, explore [CV writing services](/services/packages/cv-writing) and explain where you intend to apply.

faqs.question: Is a photo compulsory for every Sri Lankan CV?
faqs.answer: Do not assume a universal requirement. Check the specific employer and application instructions before including one.

faqs.question: Will removing a photo guarantee better results?
faqs.answer: No. It is a formatting and relevance decision. Hiring still depends on your suitability and the employer's process.

This is a practical privacy and document-design approach, not legal advice about every employer or country. Formal application forms may have separate requirements that should be assessed in their own context.
Start with information needed for contact
Your name, professional email, phone number and relevant location are usually the useful starting details. Add a LinkedIn or portfolio link when it supports the application.
A full home address often provides more detail than the reader needs at the first stage. City or region can communicate location without distributing your precise residential address widely.

An NIC or passport number is different from a contact detail. Ask why it is needed and whether a verified, secure application process requests it separately. Do not place identity-document scans inside a publicly shared CV.
Check the employer's authenticity before supplying sensitive information. A request arriving through an unverified message deserves investigation even if it uses a familiar company name.
Question unrelated personal categories

Age, religion and marital status generally do not explain professional capability. Consider whether they contribute anything necessary to evaluating the role. A template field is not evidence that the employer requires it.

For UK applications, the National Careers Service advises excluding age, date of birth, marital status and nationality from the CV. See its [official CV guidance](https://nationalcareers.service.gov.uk/careers-advice/cv-sections). Keep country-specific decisions separate from assumptions about every market.
Protect other people's information too
Referee phone numbers and email addresses belong to other people. Get permission before sharing them and consider supplying them at the stage the employer requests references.
Do not include client names, patient information or confidential internal records as proof of your work. Describe achievements in a way that respects the information you are allowed to disclose.
Maintain a shareable version

Keep a CV suitable for sending to recruiters or uploading to professional platforms. Provide additional verified information through the appropriate channel only when necessary. Review old copies so sensitive fields do not reappear during tailoring.

If you request a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review), ask the reviewer to check unnecessary personal information as well as wording and layout. A professional document should communicate value without distributing irrelevant private details.

faqs.question: What if an official form asks for information omitted from my CV?
faqs.answer: Assess the genuine form and its purpose separately. Omitting a field from a CV does not mean ignoring a legitimate application requirement.

faqs.question: Should I send my NIC with a CV writing enquiry?
faqs.answer: An initial career-writing discussion should not normally need an identity-document copy. Ask why any sensitive document is requested before sharing it.

content: Removing weak content can improve a CV more than adding another page. Review these ten items and keep only information that serves the application. Use judgment rather than deleting blindly. A detail that is irrelevant to one vacancy may be required or valuable for another.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Removing weak content can improve a CV more than adding another page. Review these ten items and keep only information that serves the application.
Use judgment rather than deleting blindly. A detail that is irrelevant to one vacancy may be required or valuable for another.
Remove vague or duplicated wording

items: **Generic objectives.** Replace statements about wanting a challenging opportunity with a relevant professional introduction.
**Unsupported adjectives.** “Exceptional” and “world-class” need evidence; often the evidence can speak more clearly on its own.
**Repeated duties.** Similar bullets across several roles can hide progression and consume space.
**Copied job descriptions.** Explain what you actually contributed, not only what the position required.

body.text: Read each paragraph and ask what new information it provides. If another section already makes the same point, combine or remove the repetition.
Remove misleading or unnecessary detail

items: **Invented results.** Replace unverifiable percentages with accurate scope or a documented deliverable.
**Skills you cannot explain.** Relevant learning can be labelled honestly; unsupported expertise should not remain.
**Unnecessary sensitive information.** Review identity numbers, personal categories and other people's contact details.
**Obsolete detail that overwhelms recent work.** Older school activities or early duties may need less space as your career develops.

body.text: Do not erase facts in a way that creates a misleading history. The aim is selective detail, not concealment.
Remove submission hazards

items: **Editing leftovers.** Delete comments, unresolved tracked changes, template instructions and highlighted reminders from the final file.
**Broken or irrelevant links.** Test portfolio and profile links, and remove destinations that are inaccessible or unrelated to the role.

body.text: A link is useful only when the reader can reach and understand the evidence. Check access permissions before using a cloud document as a portfolio example.
Rebuild the space around evidence
Use the space you recover for a clearer summary, stronger achievements or a relevant project. Do not immediately refill it with generic skills or decorative graphics.

Open the exported file after editing and inspect every page. Removing content can leave awkward gaps or headings detached from their paragraphs. Ask a reader whether the revised version makes your professional direction easier to understand.

For help deciding what deserves space, explore [CV review support](/services/packages/cv-review). If the document still reflects an earlier career stage, [CV writing services](/services/packages/cv-writing) can help restructure it around your next role.

faqs.question: Should I remove all older jobs?
faqs.answer: No. Keep an accurate chronology and relevant experience, but reduce unnecessary detail in older entries when appropriate.

faqs.question: Is every hobby irrelevant?
faqs.answer: No. A relevant activity may demonstrate useful experience, especially early in your career. Avoid including hobbies merely to fill space.

content: Having no paid work experience does not mean having no evidence for a CV. Projects, study, volunteering and practical responsibilities can demonstrate useful capabilities. The important distinction is how you label that evidence. Present student and volunteer work honestly instead of trying to make it resemble years of employment.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha
keywords: CV with no experience Sri Lanka

body.text: Having no paid work experience does not mean having no evidence for a CV. Projects, study, volunteering and practical responsibilities can demonstrate useful capabilities.
The important distinction is how you label that evidence. Present student and volunteer work honestly instead of trying to make it resemble years of employment.
Choose a realistic target

Read internship, trainee or entry-level vacancies and identify recurring requirements. Look for evidence of basic tools, communication, organisation and subject knowledge that you can actually demonstrate.
Do not apply the same opening to unrelated professions. A CV for a finance internship should highlight different projects from a CV for a social-media role.
Build the strongest sections first

Include your education with the exact qualification and completion status. Add relevant projects, technical skills and any practical experience. An unpaid society role can be useful if you explain the work rather than merely listing membership.
For a project, identify the problem, your contribution, tools used and output. “University database project” is weaker than an explanation of the records you designed and the queries you wrote.
Use everyday responsibility as evidence
Helping with a family business, coordinating an event or tutoring can demonstrate real skills. State the context accurately and avoid inventing formal job titles.

An illustrative example is organising registrations for a student event, maintaining the attendee list and coordinating updates with the organising team. This shows activity and responsibility without claiming commercial management experience.
Keep the document focused

Use a short introduction, relevant education, selected projects, practical activities and skills. Avoid a long paragraph apologising for your lack of experience. Employers recruiting beginners need evidence of readiness to learn and contribute at that level.
Remove generic skill ratings and unsupported claims. If you name Excel or Python, be prepared to explain something you have actually done with it.
Check before applying
Proofread, test links and confirm availability details requested by the employer. Ask a lecturer, supervisor or trusted reviewer to check whether the evidence matches the role.
Start with the [free career resources](/resources) or explore [student CV writing support](/services/packages/cv-writing) if you need help organising your first application.

faqs.question: Can I include unpaid work?
faqs.answer: Yes. Describe its real context and your contribution. Do not label volunteering or a university project as paid employment.

faqs.question: What if I have very few activities?
faqs.answer: Present the relevant evidence you do have clearly. Build experience through suitable projects or opportunities rather than filling the CV with invented claims.

content: A fresh graduate CV should show how your education and practical work prepare you for an entry-level role. It should not imitate a senior professional's career history. You cannot guarantee interviews, but you can make relevant evidence easier to assess. Begin with suitable vacancies and the capabilities they actually require from a beginner.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: A fresh graduate CV should show how your education and practical work prepare you for an entry-level role. It should not imitate a senior professional's career history.
You cannot guarantee interviews, but you can make relevant evidence easier to assess. Begin with suitable vacancies and the capabilities they actually require from a beginner.
Identify your strongest proof

List internships, final-year work, relevant assignments, volunteering and leadership activities. For each, record what you personally did and what you produced. A short internship can provide strong evidence if the contribution is explained clearly.
Distinguish group outputs from your own work. “Built the reporting dashboard for a group research project” is more precise than claiming the entire project as an individual achievement.
Make education informative

Include the degree, institution, completion status and useful specialisation. Add results or selected modules when they support the application. Do not let a long subject list displace practical evidence.
If you are awaiting final results, say so accurately. Do not present an expected classification as an awarded result.
Replace the generic graduate objective

Introduce your professional direction and relevant strengths. An accounting graduate might mention project work in financial analysis and an internship involving reconciliations. A computing graduate might introduce a specific technical project and the role they want.
The summary should connect to evidence lower in the CV. Avoid describing yourself as an expert because you completed an introductory course.
Prepare for the application channel
Use a readable document, familiar headings and working links. If the vacancy asks for grades, availability or a separate statement, provide those through the requested format as well.
Tailor the emphasis for each role. A graduate programme and a specialist junior position may evaluate different aspects of the same background.
Build an improvement cycle

Keep a record of applications and feedback. Update the CV when you complete a useful project or gain practical responsibility. If your target roles consistently require skills you lack, use that information to plan development rather than repeatedly changing the font.
Explore [CV writing services](/services/packages/cv-writing) for help presenting graduate evidence, or use a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) when you already have a draft.

faqs.question: Should a graduate include a part-time job unrelated to the degree?
faqs.answer: It can be useful if it demonstrates relevant responsibility or transferable skills. Explain the connection and keep the detail proportionate.

faqs.question: Do employers expect years of experience from every graduate?
faqs.answer: Requirements differ. Target genuine entry-level opportunities and read the essential criteria rather than assuming all vacancies have the same expectations.

content: An internship CV should connect your current learning with the work you are ready to support. Specific projects and clear availability make that connection easier to understand. Recruiters do not need an exaggerated career history from an intern. They need an accurate picture of your skills, preparation and suitability for the placement.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: An internship CV should connect your current learning with the work you are ready to support. Specific projects and clear availability make that connection easier to understand.
Recruiters do not need an exaggerated career history from an intern. They need an accurate picture of your skills, preparation and suitability for the placement.
Read the placement requirements

Check the discipline, required study stage, duration and application materials. Some placements have academic conditions or scheduling requirements. Confirm those facts before spending time polishing a CV for an unsuitable opening.
Where availability is requested, give realistic dates. Do not promise full-time attendance if lectures or examinations make that impossible.
Select projects that resemble the work

A finance internship may value spreadsheet analysis and careful checking. A marketing internship may value content planning and campaign reporting. Choose projects that demonstrate relevant tasks rather than listing every assignment.
Explain the problem, your contribution and the output. For example, describe how you cleaned survey data and prepared a summary for a university project, rather than writing only “research skills.”
Show how you work with others
Internship work often involves learning, asking questions and completing tasks under supervision. Evidence from group projects or volunteering can show reliability and communication.
Describe an actual responsibility, such as coordinating deadlines or maintaining shared project notes. Avoid declaring yourself a natural leader without an example.
Make the practical details easy to find

Include your qualification, institution, expected completion date and relevant tools. Link to a small, accessible portfolio where useful. Check that the link does not reveal private group files or require unexpected permission.
Use a professional email and a readable filename. The employer should not have to search for your contact details or guess which position you want.
Submit a complete application

Tailor any requested cover letter to the placement. Explain why its tasks fit your learning and what evidence shows you can contribute. Save the vacancy and the submitted documents for interview preparation.
For support with the CV, explore [student writing services](/services/packages/cv-writing). If the letter is the difficult part, see [cover letter writing](/services/packages/cover-letter-writing).

faqs.question: Should I list every university module?
faqs.answer: No. Select modules when they add relevant evidence and leave space for practical projects and responsibilities.

faqs.question: Can I apply before completing my degree?
faqs.answer: Follow the placement's eligibility requirements. State your current study stage and expected completion accurately rather than implying you have already graduated.

content: A school leaver CV should show education, practical skills and evidence of responsibility. You do not need to invent employment to create a credible first application. Choose a realistic first role, such as a trainee, assistant or entry-level position, and use its requirements to decide what belongs in the document.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: A school leaver CV should show education, practical skills and evidence of responsibility. You do not need to invent employment to create a credible first application.
Choose a realistic first role, such as a trainee, assistant or entry-level position, and use its requirements to decide what belongs in the document.
Present education accurately

Include your school, relevant examinations and results where useful or requested. Distinguish completed examinations from results you are still awaiting. Use clear qualification names and consistent dates.
You do not need to reproduce every school record. Select information that helps the employer assess the role, especially when specific subjects or grades are part of the requirements.
Identify responsibility outside employment
School clubs, sports, volunteering, event support and family-business tasks can provide examples. Explain what you actually did rather than merely listing an activity name.

An illustrative example might describe maintaining registrations for a school event and helping communicate schedule changes. That can show organisation and attention to detail without pretending it was a formal office job.
Be specific about useful skills

If you can use spreadsheets, explain the tasks you have completed. If you list languages, use an honest description of proficiency. Do not mark every language “fluent” because a template provides that option.
Short courses can be included when relevant, with the provider and completion status. Watching a tutorial is not the same as earning a certification.
Keep the opening simple
State that you are a school leaver seeking a relevant first opportunity and name the strengths supported by the CV. Avoid a long motivational paragraph that says little about your preparation.
Use a professional email, a current phone number and appropriate location information. Avoid adding identity numbers or extensive personal details just because an old example includes them.
Ask for a careful review

Have a trusted adult, teacher or reviewer check spelling, dates and clarity. Get permission before naming someone as a referee, and share their contact details only when appropriate to the application.
Begin with [free career resources](/resources). If you need help arranging the evidence, explore [CV writing support](/services/packages/cv-writing) and explain that this is your first application.

faqs.question: Can my CV be only one page?
faqs.answer: Yes. One readable page of relevant information is better than extra pages filled with generic statements.

faqs.question: Should I include work in my family's shop?
faqs.answer: Yes, if it is relevant and described honestly. State the context and tasks instead of inventing a senior title.

Choose evidence relevant to the role you want. The aim is to make your preparation understandable without presenting academic work as professional employment.
Map activities to capabilities

List projects, presentations, research, society work and practical placements. Ask what each required you to do. A research assignment may demonstrate data collection and analysis; an event role may demonstrate scheduling and coordination.
Avoid translating every activity into leadership. Sometimes the strongest evidence is careful execution, technical problem-solving or reliable support.
Describe your personal contribution
For group work, separate the shared goal from your responsibility. Explain the part you designed, analysed or delivered and how it connected to the group output.

For example, “prepared the data-cleaning worksheet and summary charts for a group consumer-research project” is clearer than “completed a successful research project.” Add tools and methods only if you used them.
Select evidence for the application

A university society position may be valuable for an operations internship if you coordinated people and deadlines. The same role might need less space on a technical CV where a software project provides stronger evidence.
Keep a private evidence bank so you can choose different examples without changing the facts. Tailoring should change emphasis, not create a different history.
Present education and learning honestly
State the qualification, institution and expected completion. Include relevant modules or results when useful, but avoid overwhelming the CV with a transcript-like list.
Label certifications separately from informal learning. If a project is ongoing, describe completed work and current status rather than claiming a finished result.

Link to selected work when you have permission to share it. Add a short explanation so the reader understands the context and your role. Remove private data, group members' personal information and material your university or client has not authorised for publication.

Use a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) to check whether the evidence supports your target. [Student CV writing](/services/packages/cv-writing) can help organise a draft when your experience is spread across several activities.

faqs.question: Can society membership go on my CV?
faqs.answer: It can, but actual responsibilities or contributions are more informative than membership alone. Prioritise activities that support the application.

faqs.question: Should I include an unfinished project?
faqs.answer: Yes, when relevant and clearly labelled as ongoing. Describe what you have completed and avoid presenting expected outcomes as achieved results.

Choose projects for relevance
Select projects that connect to the vacancy. A data-analysis project may deserve more space for an analyst role, while a scheduling or process-design project may suit operations work.

Give one project enough explanation

Instead of listing six unexplained projects, describe a few relevant ones well. Explain the problem, your role, tools and output. Include a limitation when it helps distinguish a prototype from a finished product.

An illustrative marketing example might describe developing a content calendar for a university initiative and reviewing engagement patterns. Do not invent commercial campaign results for work that never involved a paying client.
Show evidence of reliability
Use an example of meeting a deadline, checking data, coordinating a group or responding to feedback. Explain the behaviour rather than simply listing “time management” and “teamwork.”
If you held a society role, distinguish the title from the contribution. Organising the registration process is more informative than naming a committee position without context.
Make a small portfolio useful

Where relevant, share a few selected outputs with short descriptions. Check that the links open and that you have permission to publish the material. Remove personal information and private group files.
A repository or design gallery is stronger when the reader can understand what you contributed. Do not assume screenshots alone explain the project.
Edit the generic material out

Remove copied objectives, unsupported proficiency ratings and repetitive subject lists. Keep contact details, study status and requested availability clear. Use a simple layout that gives evidence room to breathe.

Before submission, ask a reviewer what they learned about you that would not apply to every classmate. If the answer is little, add more specific evidence. Explore [student CV writing](/services/packages/cv-writing) or a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) for help with that editing process.

faqs.question: Do I need a creative design to stand out?
faqs.answer: No. Relevant, specific examples and clear writing can distinguish your application within a simple professional layout.

faqs.question: Can I reuse a classmate's wording?
faqs.answer: Use examples to understand structure, but write about your own contribution. Shared wording can introduce claims that do not describe your experience.

This process creates a document you can update as your career develops. It also gives you a useful record for cover letters, applications and interviews.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Your first professional CV should turn your education and practical activities into a focused case for an entry-level role. Begin with evidence rather than a blank template.
This process creates a document you can update as your career develops. It also gives you a useful record for cover letters, applications and interviews.
Build your source record
Gather qualification details, internship dates, project notes, relevant training and activities where you held responsibility. Record your contribution and output for each example.
Keep the source record private and complete. The application CV will be more selective. Resolve uncertain dates and result claims before copying them into several documents.
Choose your first role family
Read suitable vacancies and identify the skills they need. Select opportunities appropriate to your preparation rather than trying to target every profession in one CV.
For related roles, you can maintain a common base and change the emphasis. For substantially different directions, you may need different project selections and summaries.
Write the main sections
Include contact information, a concise introduction, education, relevant projects, internships or practical work, and skills. Add certifications or activities when they support the target.

Explain project work through the problem, your contribution, tools and output. Describe internships through tasks performed and evidence of learning or contribution. Do not substitute generic adjectives for those details.
Check the professional details

Use an email address you monitor, a correct phone number and working portfolio links. State whether your qualification is completed or ongoing. Ask referees before sharing their details and avoid unnecessary sensitive personal information.
Use readable formatting and consistent dates. Open the export and inspect every page, including the final page where awkward breaks are easy to miss.
Prepare the rest of the application

Tailor any requested cover letter and complete application fields accurately. Align dates and titles with LinkedIn. Save the vacancy and the submitted CV so interview preparation uses the same evidence.
After each useful project or placement, update the master record. Review feedback for patterns, but do not assume every rejection means the document is wrong.

faqs.question: Should I wait until graduation to prepare a CV?
faqs.answer: No. Prepare it when you begin seeking suitable opportunities and state your expected completion accurately.

faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Identify the area where you need help and choose support according to your application needs and budget.

content: With several years of experience, your CV should show how your contribution has developed. A longer list of duties alone does not communicate professional progression. Choose the next role you want and explain the experience that prepares you for it. Keep your history accurate while giving more space to recent, relevant work.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: With several years of experience, your CV should show how your contribution has developed. A longer list of duties alone does not communicate professional progression.
Choose the next role you want and explain the experience that prepares you for it. Keep your history accurate while giving more space to recent, relevant work.
Identify your professional direction

Decide whether you are deepening a specialism, moving into management or changing function. Each direction requires different evidence. An application for a senior technical role should not be written as if people management is the only form of advancement.
Use the summary to introduce that direction through capabilities you already demonstrate, not through a title you hope to hold.
Show growth within the experience section

Look for increased independence, more complex work, larger scope or responsibility for others. Explain promotions with separate titles and dates. If your title stayed the same, describe how the work changed.
For example, moving from preparing a report to owning its quality checks and presenting findings shows development. You do not need to invent a promotion to make that progression visible.
Select evidence rather than repeating duties

Give recent roles enough context and selected achievements. Reduce repetitive detail in earlier roles while preserving the chronology. A first job may need only a concise entry if its duties no longer support the target.
Use results you can verify and explain your contribution to team outcomes. Where numbers are unavailable, describe delivered improvements, scope or complexity.
Update education and skills priorities

Relevant professional work may now deserve more prominence than school details. Keep qualifications accurate and add current certifications where useful. Remove obsolete tools that distract from the role you want.
Skills should reflect work you can discuss at interview. Do not leave an introductory course labelled as expertise simply because it has been on the CV for years.
Make the next step credible

Read the CV beside a representative vacancy. Identify where the evidence supports its responsibilities and where a genuine gap remains. Use that review to improve both the document and your target selection.
Explore [professional CV writing](/services/packages/cv-writing) if your CV still reads like an entry-level application, or request a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) for focused feedback.

faqs.question: Should I remove my first job?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Keep an accurate history and useful evidence, but reduce detail when recent roles are more relevant.

faqs.question: Can progression be shown without promotions?
faqs.answer: Yes. Greater scope, independence, technical depth and responsibility can demonstrate development even when the official title did not change.

title: Executive CV Writing: Why Senior Professionals Need a Different CV Strategy
excerpt: An executive CV should make leadership scope, decisions and business contribution clear. A long operational history does not automatically demonstrate executive readiness.…
content: An executive CV should make leadership scope, decisions and business contribution clear. A long operational history does not automatically demonstrate executive readiness. The reader needs context for the scale of your responsibility and evidence of how you exercised it. Keep claims proportionate to your actual authority and involvement.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: An executive CV should make leadership scope, decisions and business contribution clear. A long operational history does not automatically demonstrate executive readiness.
The reader needs context for the scale of your responsibility and evidence of how you exercised it. Keep claims proportionate to your actual authority and involvement.
Establish the operating context

Explain the business environment, function or region you led. Include team, budget or operational scope when accurate and appropriate to disclose. Distinguish direct accountability from participation or advisory responsibility.
“Supported a transformation programme” and “held executive accountability for the programme” describe different roles. Use the one that matches the facts.
Select consequential decisions
Identify changes you led, priorities you set or difficult trade-offs you managed. Explain the action and result without turning each bullet into a lengthy case study.

An example might describe redesigning an operating model and establishing governance for implementation. Add verified business outcomes where available, while distinguishing the team's delivery from your leadership contribution.
Make achievements comparable

Revenue growth, cost reduction and delivery improvements need context. State the period, baseline or business scope when needed to avoid misleading comparisons. Do not mix forecast benefits with realised results.
For confidential work, use appropriately general descriptions or authorised ranges. A CV should not disclose sensitive customer or commercial information merely to sound impressive.
Reduce detail that obscures seniority

Routine duties can establish context briefly, but should not dominate the document. Give more space to leadership, strategic decisions, risk management and organisational outcomes relevant to the target.
Keep earlier roles concise while showing the progression that led to current responsibility. A selective history is different from an incomplete or misleading one.
Align supporting materials
Your LinkedIn profile, executive biography and CV should agree on titles, dates and major claims. They may differ in length and tone, but should communicate a consistent professional identity.

For support with this level of positioning, explore [executive CV writing options](/services/packages/cv-writing). Bring context and verified evidence rather than expecting a writer to infer leadership scope from your title alone.

faqs.question: Does an executive CV need a different design?
faqs.answer: It needs an appropriate emphasis and clear hierarchy. Restrained formatting can work well; strategic content matters more than decorative seniority cues.

faqs.question: Should every achievement use financial metrics?
faqs.answer: No. Governance, quality, capability building and delivery can be relevant. Explain the evidence and business significance accurately.

title: How to Write a Manager-Level CV That Shows Leadership, Not Just Responsibilities
excerpt: A manager-level CV should explain how you directed work, supported people and handled decisions. “Managed a team” is a starting point, not sufficient evidence. Show the…
content: A manager-level CV should explain how you directed work, supported people and handled decisions. “Managed a team” is a starting point, not sufficient evidence. Show the scope of your responsibility and the actions that influenced delivery. Be clear about whether you formally managed people, coordinated colleagues or led a temporary project.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: A manager-level CV should explain how you directed work, supported people and handled decisions. “Managed a team” is a starting point, not sufficient evidence.
Show the scope of your responsibility and the actions that influenced delivery. Be clear about whether you formally managed people, coordinated colleagues or led a temporary project.
Establish the team context
Describe the function, team structure and your authority. Include team size or operational scope when accurate and useful. Distinguish direct reports from people you influenced through coordination.

This context helps a reader interpret your achievements. Leading a small specialist team can involve different challenges from supervising a large shift operation; neither should be described vaguely.
Explain leadership through actions
Look for examples of setting priorities, allocating work, coaching, resolving escalations and improving handovers. Describe what you did and why it was needed.

An illustrative bullet might explain introducing a weekly workload review to identify overdue tasks and agree responsibilities. Add an outcome only if you can support it; implementing a meeting is not automatically proof of improved productivity.
Show judgment as well as activity
Managers make trade-offs involving time, quality, people and resources. Select an example where you evaluated options and guided a decision. Keep confidential personnel details out of the CV.
Avoid blaming former colleagues or employers. Describe the challenge professionally and focus on your contribution to the response.
Connect people management to delivery
Training and coaching become more meaningful when the reader understands their purpose. Explain whether you helped colleagues adopt a system, improve a process or take on new responsibilities.
Do not claim sole credit for team performance. State your leadership contribution and the result at the appropriate level.
Position the next management step
Compare your evidence with the target role's scope. If you are moving into management for the first time, present relevant coordination and mentoring honestly without changing your official title.

A [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) can help identify missing leadership evidence. Explore [professional CV writing](/services/packages/cv-writing) when your current document still consists mainly of operational duties.

faqs.question: Can I show leadership without direct reports?
faqs.answer: Yes. Project leadership, mentoring and coordination can be relevant. Describe the actual authority and context rather than implying formal line management.

faqs.question: Should I list team size in every role?
faqs.answer: Include it when it helps explain scope and is accurate. Team size alone does not establish the quality of your leadership.

If every role contains the same duties, the reader may struggle to see progression. Review the history for meaningful changes rather than simply adding another job entry.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: Ten years of employment does not explain how your professional contribution developed. Your CV should show the changes in scope, responsibility and capability across that time.
If every role contains the same duties, the reader may struggle to see progression. Review the history for meaningful changes rather than simply adding another job entry.
Map the turning points

Identify promotions, changes of function, more complex projects and increased responsibility. Note when you became accountable for decisions, quality, customers or colleagues that you previously supported.
Career progression is not always upward movement in titles. Deeper technical expertise, broader industry exposure or a deliberate specialist move can also be important.
Give each role a distinct purpose

Use a short context statement and selected evidence for each relevant position. Avoid copying the same bullet list under every employer. Explain what was different about the environment or your contribution.

For example, an early role might involve preparing schedules, while a later role involves coordinating several teams and resolving resource conflicts. That difference should be visible in the wording.
Show promotions clearly

Keep official titles and date ranges. If several roles were with one employer, group them under the organisation while giving each position a clear entry. Do not merge the dates so it appears you held the highest title for the entire period.
Explain meaningful changes in responsibility under the relevant role rather than repeating the employer description.
Reduce older detail thoughtfully
Recent relevant experience often deserves more space. Older roles can be shorter while preserving the career chronology. Keep an older achievement when it remains particularly relevant to the target.
Do not remove information solely to hide a career gap or a lateral move. A coherent, accurate history is more useful than an artificially smooth narrative.
Connect the past to the next role
Write the summary after reviewing the progression. It should explain your current professional value, not repeat an objective written at the start of your career.

Ask a reader what changed between your first and most recent roles. If they cannot tell, refine the evidence. [Professional CV writing](/services/packages/cv-writing) or a [CV review](/services/packages/cv-review) can help restructure an accumulated document around the career you now have.

faqs.question: Must every career move look like a promotion?
faqs.answer: No. Lateral moves, specialisation and industry changes can be valuable. Explain the actual contribution and context honestly.

faqs.question: Should I mention an old achievement?
faqs.answer: Yes, when it remains relevant and adds distinct evidence. Keep it proportionate so it does not overwhelm recent work.

title: Executive CV vs Regular CV: What Actually Changes?

content: An executive CV uses many of the same basic sections as other professional CVs. What changes is the level of context, accountability and impact the evidence must explain. The distinction is not a more expensive-looking template. It is a clearer account of decisions and responsibility at the level of the role you are targeting.
author: Chanuka Jeewantha

body.text: An executive CV uses many of the same basic sections as other professional CVs. What changes is the level of context, accountability and impact the evidence must explain.
The distinction is not a more expensive-looking template. It is a clearer account of decisions and responsibility at the level of the role you are targeting.
The opening describes leadership scope

A general professional profile may introduce a function and technical strengths. An executive profile should also make the leadership environment understandable: business scope, strategic responsibilities and relevant areas of transformation or growth.
Avoid filling the opening with broad claims such as visionary or transformational. Show why those descriptions would be justified through the evidence that follows.
Experience focuses on consequential contribution

Operational tasks can establish context, but executive entries should explain significant priorities, decisions and outcomes. What did you lead? What authority did you hold? What changed under your responsibility?
Distinguish executive accountability from advisory or project involvement. The reader should not have to guess whether you made a decision, recommended it or implemented one part of it.
Metrics require context

Business results can be persuasive when the period, baseline and scope are clear. Do not present forecast savings as realised savings or company-wide growth as an individual result without explanation.
Some contributions are better demonstrated through governance changes, delivery milestones or capability development. Financial metrics are not the only valid evidence.
Supporting experience becomes more selective

Earlier roles establish progression, but do not need equal detail. Education remains accurate and visible while recent leadership work takes priority. Include board, advisory or professional appointments only when genuine and relevant.
Keep confidential information appropriately general. An executive CV is a career document, not permission to publish internal strategy or sensitive client data.
Consistency extends beyond the CV
Compare the CV with your LinkedIn profile and executive biography. Titles, dates and major claims should agree, even when the documents serve different audiences.

If you are moving toward executive responsibility, show the evidence you have without pretending the transition is already complete. Explore [senior and executive CV writing support](/services/packages/cv-writing) for help positioning the actual scope of your career.

faqs.question: Is an executive CV always longer?
faqs.answer: No. Length depends on the evidence and application requirements. Selective, clear leadership examples matter more than additional pages.

faqs.question: Can a manager use an executive-style summary?
faqs.answer: Use a summary appropriate to your actual scope and target. Do not imply enterprise authority or board responsibility you have not held.
